158.m: Brahmā said: / They said to that best of sages: “Who is designated as the giver of knowledge? / Is it Brahmā, Viṣṇu, or Maheśa, or Āditya, or the Moon?

158.s:
agniś ca varuṇaḥ kaḥ syāj jñānado munisattama
agastyaḥ punar apy āha jñānadaḥ śrūyatām ayam //
158.d:
अग्निश् च वरुणः कः स्याज् ज्ञानदो मुनिसत्तम
अगस्त्यः पुनर् अप्य् आह ज्ञानदः श्रूयताम् अयम् ॥
158.m: Or Agni, or Varuṇa—who might be the giver of knowledge, O best of sages?” / Agastya spoke yet again: “Hear who this giver of knowledge is.

158.s:
yā āpaḥ so 'gnir ity ukto yo 'gniḥ sūryaḥ sa ucyate
yaś ca sūryaḥ sa vai viṣṇur yaś ca viṣṇuḥ sa bhāskaraḥ //
158.d:
या आपः सो ऽग्निर् इत्य् उक्तो यो ऽग्निः सूर्यः स उच्यते
यश् च सूर्यः स वै विष्णुर् यश् च विष्णुः स भास्करः ॥
158.m: That which is the waters, he is called Agni; he who is Agni, he is called Sūrya; / and he who is Sūrya, he indeed is Viṣṇu; and he who is Viṣṇu, he is the Sun;

158.s:
yaś ca brahmā sa vai rudro yo rudraḥ sarvam eva tat
yasya sarvaṃ tu taj jñānaṃ jñānadaḥ so 'tra kīrtyate //
158.d:
यश् च ब्रह्मा स वै रुद्रो यो रुद्रः सर्वम् एव तत्
यस्य सर्वं तु तज् ज्ञानं ज्ञानदः सो ऽत्र कीर्त्यते ॥
158.m: and he who is Brahmā, he indeed is Rudra; he who is Rudra is all this. / He whose knowledge all this is, he is proclaimed here as the giver of knowledge.

158.s:
deśikaprerakavyākhyākṛdupādhyāyadehadāḥ
guravaḥ santi bahavas teṣāṃ jñānaprado mahān //
158.d:
देशिकप्रेरकव्याख्याकृदुपाध्यायदेहदाः
गुरवः सन्ति बहवस् तेषां ज्ञानप्रदो महान् ॥
158.m: The guide, the prompter, the commentator, the teacher, the giver of the body— / there are many gurus; among them, the giver of knowledge is the greatest.

158.s:
tad eva jñānam atroktaṃ yena bhedo vihanyate
eka evādvayaḥ śaṃbhur indramitrāgnināmabhiḥ
vadanti bahudhā viprā bhrāntopakṛtihetave //
158.d:
तद् एव ज्ञानम् अत्रोक्तं येन भेदो विहन्यते
एक एवाद्वयः शंभुर् इन्द्रमित्राग्निनामभिः
वदन्ति बहुधा विप्रा भ्रान्तोपकृतिहेतवे ॥
158.m: That alone is spoken of here as knowledge by which difference is destroyed. / Śaṃbhu is one alone, without a second; under the names of Indra, Mitra, and Agni / the twice-born speak of him variously, for the sake of helping the deluded.”

158.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā muner vākyaṃ gāthā gāyanta eva te
jagmuḥ pañcottarāṃ gaṅgāṃ pañca jagmuś ca dakṣiṇām //
158.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा मुनेर् वाक्यं गाथा गायन्त एव ते
जग्मुः पञ्चोत्तरां गङ्गां पञ्च जग्मुश् च दक्षिणाम् ॥
158.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard these words of the sage, singing songs, / five went to the northern Gaṅgā, and five went to the southern [Gaṅgā],

158.s:
agastyenoditān devān pūjayanto yathāvidhi
āsaneṣu viśeṣeṇa hy āsīnās tattvacintakāḥ //
158.d:
अगस्त्येनोदितान् देवान् पूजयन्तो यथाविधि
आसनेषु विशेषेण ह्य् आसीनास् तत्त्वचिन्तकाः ॥
158.m: worshipping according to rule the deities spoken of by Agastya, / especially seated upon their seats, contemplating ultimate reality.

158.s:
teṣāṃ sarve suragaṇāḥ prītimanto 'bhavan mune
sraṣṭṛtvaṃ tu yugādau yat kalpitaṃ viśvayoninā //
158.d:
तेषां सर्वे सुरगणाः प्रीतिमन्तो ऽभवन् मुने
स्रष्टृत्वं तु युगादौ यत् कल्पितं विश्वयोनिना ॥
158.m: All the hosts of gods were pleased with them, O sage. / The status of creator which was fashioned at the beginning of the yuga by the womb of the universe—

158.s:
adharmāṇāṃ nivṛttyarthaṃ vedānāṃ sthāpanāya ca
lokānām upakārārthaṃ dharmakāmārthasiddhaye //
158.d:
अधर्माणां निवृत्त्यर्थं वेदानां स्थापनाय च
लोकानाम् उपकारार्थं धर्मकामार्थसिद्धये ॥
158.m: for the cessation of unrighteousness and the establishment of the Vedas, / for the welfare of the worlds, for the attainment of dharma, desire, and wealth,

158.s:
purāṇasmṛtivedārthadharmaśāstrārthaniścaye
sraṣṭṛtvaṃ jagatām iṣṭaṃ tādṛgrūpā bhaviṣyatha //
158.d:
पुराणस्मृतिवेदार्थधर्मशास्त्रार्थनिश्चये
स्रष्टृत्वं जगताम् इष्टं तादृग्रूपा भविष्यथ ॥
158.m: and for determining the meaning of the Purāṇas, Smṛtis, Vedas, and treatises on dharma— / the status of creator of the worlds was desired; of such form you shall become.

158.s:
prajāpatitvaṃ teṣāṃ vai bhaviṣyati śanaiḥ kramāt
yadā hy adharmo bhavitā vedānāṃ ca parābhavaḥ //
158.d:
प्रजापतित्वं तेषां वै भविष्यति शनैः क्रमात्
यदा ह्य् अधर्मो भविता वेदानां च पराभवः ॥
158.m: The status of prajāpatis shall indeed be theirs gradually, in due course. / For whenever there shall be unrighteousness and the decline of the Vedas,

158.s:
vedānāṃ vyasanaṃ tebhyo bhāvivyāsās tatas tu te
yadā yadā tu dharmasya glānir vedasya dṛśyate //
158.d:
वेदानां व्यसनं तेभ्यो भाविव्यासास् ततस् तु ते
यदा यदा तु धर्मस्य ग्लानिर् वेदस्य दृश्यते ॥
158.m: the arrangement of the Vedas [shall proceed] from them; therefore they are the future Vyāsas. / Whenever there is seen a decline of dharma and of the Veda,

158.s:
tadā tadā tu te vyāsā bhaviṣyanty upakāriṇaḥ
teṣāṃ yat tapasaḥ sthānaṃ gaṅgāyās tīram uttamam //
158.d:
तदा तदा तु ते व्यासा भविष्यन्त्य् उपकारिणः
तेषां यत् तपसः स्थानं गङ्गायास् तीरम् उत्तमम् ॥
158.m: then and then these Vyāsas, benefactors, will appear. / Their place of austerity, that excellent bank of the Gaṅgā—

158.s:
tatra tatra śivo viṣṇur aham āditya eva ca
agnir āpaḥ sarvam iti tatra saṃnihitaṃ sadā //
158.d:
तत्र तत्र शिवो विष्णुर् अहम् आदित्य एव च
अग्निर् आपः सर्वम् इति तत्र संनिहितं सदा ॥
158.m: in each such place Śiva, Viṣṇu, I, and Āditya, / Agni, the waters—all that is ever present there.

158.s:
naitebhyaḥ pāvanaṃ kiṃcin naitebhyas tv adhikaṃ kvacit
tattadākāratāṃ prāptaṃ paraṃ brahmaiva kevalam //
158.d:
नैतेभ्यः पावनं किंचिन् नैतेभ्यस् त्व् अधिकं क्वचित्
तत्तदाकारतां प्राप्तं परं ब्रह्मैव केवलम् ॥
158.m: Nothing is more purifying than these; nowhere is anything greater than these. / It is merely the Supreme Brahman alone that has assumed each particular form.

158.s:
sarvātmakaḥ śivo vyāpī sarvabhāvasvarūpadhṛk
viśeṣatas tatra tīrthe sarvaprāṇyanukampayā //
158.d:
सर्वात्मकः शिवो व्यापी सर्वभावस्वरूपधृक्
विशेषतस् तत्र तीर्थे सर्वप्राण्यनुकम्पया ॥
158.m: Śiva is the self of all, all-pervading, holding the form of every state of being, / especially at that holy ford, out of compassion for all living beings,

158.s:
sarvair devair anuvṛtas tadanugrahakārakaḥ
dharmavyāsās tu te jñeyā vedavyāsās tathaiva ca //
158.d:
सर्वैर् देवैर् अनुवृतस् तदनुग्रहकारकः
धर्मव्यासास् तु ते ज्ञेया वेदव्यासास् तथैव च ॥
158.m: accompanied by all the gods, causing grace to them. / They are to be known as Dharma-Vyāsas and likewise as Veda-Vyāsas.

158.s:
teṣāṃ tīrthaṃ tena nāmnā vyapadiṣṭaṃ jagattraye
pāpapaṅkakṣālanāmbho mohadhvāntamadāpaham
sarvasiddhipradaṃ puṃsāṃ vyāsatīrtham anuttamam //
158.d:
तेषां तीर्थं तेन नाम्ना व्यपदिष्टं जगत्त्रये
पापपङ्कक्षालनाम्भो मोहध्वान्तमदापहम्
सर्वसिद्धिप्रदं पुंसां व्यासतीर्थम् अनुत्तमम् ॥
158.m: Their holy ford is designated by that name throughout the three worlds: / water for washing away the mud of sin, removing the arrogance of the darkness of delusion, / granting all perfections to men—the unsurpassed Vyāsatīrtha.

159.s:
brahmovāca
vañjarāsaṃgamaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam
ṛṣibhiḥ sevitaṃ nityaṃ siddhai rājarṣibhis tathā //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
वञ्जरासंगमं नाम तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्
ऋषिभिः सेवितं नित्यं सिद्धै राजर्षिभिस् तथा ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / The holy ford named the confluence of the Vañjarā is famed throughout the three worlds, / ever frequented by sages, by accomplished ones, and by royal sages.

159.s:
dāsatvam agamat pūrvaṃ nāgānāṃ garuḍaḥ khagaḥ
mātṛdāsyāt tadā duḥkhaparisaṃtaptamānasaḥ
kadācic cintayām āsa rahaḥ sthitvā viniśvasan //
159.d:
दासत्वम् अगमत् पूर्वं नागानां गरुडः खगः
मातृदास्यात् तदा दुःखपरिसंतप्तमानसः
कदाचिच् चिन्तयाम् आस रहः स्थित्वा विनिश्वसन् ॥
159.m: Formerly Garuḍa, the bird, fell into servitude to the serpents / through his mother’s servitude; then, his mind scorched with sorrow, / he once reflected, sighing as he stood in solitude:

159.s:
garuḍa uvāca
ta eva dhanyā loke 'smin kṛtapuṇyās ta eva hi
nānyasevā kṛtā yais tu na yeṣāṃ vyasanāgamaḥ //
159.d:
गरुड उवाच
त एव धन्या लोके ऽस्मिन् कृतपुण्यास् त एव हि
नान्यसेवा कृता यैस् तु न येषां व्यसनागमः ॥
159.m: Garuḍa said: / “They alone are fortunate in this world, they alone indeed have performed meritorious deeds, / by whom service to another was never done, to whom the arrival of misfortune does not come.

159.s:
sukhaṃ tiṣṭhanti gāyanti svapanti ca hasanti ca
svadehaprabhavo dhanyā dhig dhig anyavaśe sthitān //
159.d:
सुखं तिष्ठन्ति गायन्ति स्वपन्ति च हसन्ति च
स्वदेहप्रभवो धन्या धिग् धिग् अन्यवशे स्थितान् ॥
159.m: They abide happily, they sing, they sleep, and they laugh, / master of their own bodies, fortunate! Fie, fie upon those who abide under the control of another!”

159.s:
brahmovāca
iti cintāsamāviṣṭo jananīm etya duḥkhitaḥ
paryapṛcchad ameyātmā vainateyo 'tha mātaram //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इति चिन्तासमाविष्टो जननीम् एत्य दुःखितः
पर्यपृच्छद् अमेयात्मा वैनतेयो ऽथ मातरम् ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Engrossed thus in reflection, grieved, the son of Vinatā / of immeasurable spirit approached his mother and asked her:

159.s:
garuḍa uvāca
kasyāparādhān mātas tvaṃ pitur vā mama vānyataḥ
dāsītvam āptā vada tatkāraṇaṃ mama pṛcchataḥ //
159.d:
गरुड उवाच
कस्यापराधान् मातस् त्वं पितुर् वा मम वान्यतः
दासीत्वम् आप्ता वद तत्कारणं मम पृच्छतः ॥
159.m: Garuḍa said: / “By whose fault, mother—of father, or of mine, or of someone else— / have you obtained servitude? Tell the cause of that to me who am asking.”

159.s:
brahmovāca
sābravīt putram ātmīyam aruṇasyānujaṃ priyam //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
साब्रवीत् पुत्रम् आत्मीयम् अरुणस्यानुजं प्रियम् ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / She spoke to her own son, the beloved younger brother of Aruṇa:

159.s:
vinatovāca
naiva kasyāparādho 'sti svāparādho mayoditaḥ
yasyā vākyaṃ viparyeti sā dāsī syān mayoditam //
159.d:
विनतोवाच
नैव कस्यापराधो ऽस्ति स्वापराधो मयोदितः
यस्या वाक्यं विपर्येति सा दासी स्यान् मयोदितम् ॥
159.m: Vinatā said: / “It is not anyone else’s fault; it was my own fault declared by me: / ‘She whose statement turns out false shall become a slave’—so it was said by me.

159.s:
kadrūś cāpi tathaivāhaṃ sā mayā saṃyutā yayau
kadrvā mamābhavad vādaś chadmanāhaṃ tayā jitā //
159.d:
कद्रूश् चापि तथैवाहं सा मया संयुता ययौ
कद्र्वा ममाभवद् वादश् छद्मनाहं तया जिता ॥
159.m: Kadrū and I were likewise [in agreement]; she went together with me. / A dispute arose between Kadrū and me; by trickery I was defeated by her.

159.s:
vidhir hi balavāṃs tāta kāṃ kāṃ ceṣṭāṃ na ceṣṭate
evaṃ dāsītvam agamaṃ kadrvāḥ kaśyapanandana
yadā dāsī tu jātāhaṃ dāso 'bhūs tvaṃ dvijanmaja //
159.d:
विधिर् हि बलवांस् तात कां कां चेष्टां न चेष्टते
एवं दासीत्वम् अगमं कद्र्वाः कश्यपनन्दन
यदा दासी तु जाताहं दासो ऽभूस् त्वं द्विजन्मज ॥
159.m: For destiny is powerful, dear child; what action does it not perform? / Thus I fell into servitude to Kadrū, O son of Kaśyapa. / When I became a slave, you became a slave, O twice-born son.”

159.s:
brahmovāca
tūṣṇīṃ tadā babhūvāsau garuḍo 'tīva duḥkhitaḥ
na kiṃcid ūce jananīṃ cintayan bhavitavyatām //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तूष्णीं तदा बभूवासौ गरुडो ऽतीव दुःखितः
न किंचिद् ऊचे जननीं चिन्तयन् भवितव्यताम् ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Then Garuḍa became silent, exceedingly sorrowful; / he said nothing to his mother, reflecting upon the inevitability of destiny.

159.s:
kadrūḥ kadācit sā prāha putrāṇāṃ hitam icchatī
ātmano bhūtim icchantī vinatāṃ khagamātaram //
159.d:
कद्रूः कदाचित् सा प्राह पुत्राणां हितम् इच्छती
आत्मनो भूतिम् इच्छन्ती विनतां खगमातरम् ॥
159.m: Kadrū, desiring the welfare of her sons and desiring her own prosperity, / once spoke to Vinatā, the mother of the bird:

159.s:
kadrūr uvāca
putraḥ sūryaṃ namaskartuṃ tava yāty anivāritaḥ
aho lokatraye 'py asmin dhanyāsi bata dāsy api //
159.d:
कद्रूर् उवाच
पुत्रः सूर्यं नमस्कर्तुं तव यात्य् अनिवारितः
अहो लोकत्रये ऽप्य् अस्मिन् धन्यासि बत दास्य् अपि ॥
159.m: Kadrū said: / “Your son goes unobstructed to pay homage to the Sun. / Ah, in this threefold world you are fortunate indeed, even though a slave!”

159.s:
brahmovāca
svaduḥkhaṃ gūhamānā sā kadrūṃ prāha suvismitā //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स्वदुःखं गूहमाना सा कद्रूं प्राह सुविस्मिता ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Concealing her own sorrow, highly astonished, she spoke to Kadrū:

159.s:
vinatovāca
tava putrās tu kim iti raviṃ draṣṭuṃ na yānti ca //
159.d:
विनतोवाच
तव पुत्रास् तु किम् इति रविं द्रष्टुं न यान्ति च ॥
159.m: Vinatā said: / “Why is it that your sons do not go to see the Sun?”

159.s:
kadrūr uvāca
putrān madīyān subhage naya nāgālayaṃ prati
samudrasya samīpe tu tad āste śītalaṃ saraḥ //
159.d:
कद्रूर् उवाच
पुत्रान् मदीयान् सुभगे नय नागालयं प्रति
समुद्रस्य समीपे तु तद् आस्ते शीतलं सरः ॥
159.m: Kadrū said: / “O fortunate woman, carry my sons toward the abode of serpents; / near the ocean there lies that cool lake.”

159.s:
brahmovāca
suparṇas tv avahan nāgān kadrūṃ ca vinatā tathā
tataḥ provāca muditā vainateyasya mātaram //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सुपर्णस् त्व् अवहन् नागान् कद्रूं च विनता तथा
ततः प्रोवाच मुदिता वैनतेयस्य मातरम् ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Then the fair-feathered one carried the serpents, and Vinatā [carried] Kadrū. / Thereupon, delighted, she spoke to the mother of the son of Vinatā:

159.s:
surāṇāṃ netu nilayaṃ garuḍo matsutān iti
punaḥ prāha sarpamātā garuḍaṃ vinayānvitam //
159.d:
सुराणां नेतु निलयं गरुडो मत्सुतान् इति
पुनः प्राह सर्पमाता गरुडं विनयान्वितम् ॥
159.m: “Let Garuḍa carry my sons to the abode of the gods.” / Then the mother of snakes spoke again to Garuḍa, who was full of humility:

159.s:
sarpamātovāca
putrā me draṣṭum icchanti haṃsaṃ trijagatāṃ gurum
namaskṛtvā tataḥ sūryam eṣyanti nilayaṃ mama
haṇḍe tvaṃ naya putrān me sūryamaṇḍalam anvaham //
159.d:
सर्पमातोवाच
पुत्रा मे द्रष्टुम् इच्छन्ति हंसं त्रिजगतां गुरुम्
नमस्कृत्वा ततः सूर्यम् एष्यन्ति निलयं मम
हण्डे त्वं नय पुत्रान् मे सूर्यमण्डलम् अन्वहम् ॥
159.m: The mother of snakes said: / “My sons wish to see the swan, the guru of the three worlds; / having paid homage to the Sun, they will then come to my abode. / Ho there! Carry my sons daily to the orb of the Sun.”

159.s:
brahmovāca
sā vepamānā vinatā dīnā kadrūm abhāṣata //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सा वेपमाना विनता दीना कद्रूम् अभाषत ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Trembling, miserable Vinatā spoke to Kadrū:

159.s:
vinatovāca
nāhaṃ kṣamā sarpamātaḥ putro me neṣyate sutān
dṛṣṭvā dinakaraṃ devaṃ punar eva prayāntu te //
159.d:
विनतोवाच
नाहं क्षमा सर्पमातः पुत्रो मे नेष्यते सुतान्
दृष्ट्वा दिनकरं देवं पुनर् एव प्रयान्तु ते ॥
159.m: Vinatā said: / “I am not capable, O mother of serpents; my son shall carry your sons. / Having seen the divine maker of day, let them return again.”

159.s:
brahmovāca
vinatā svasutaṃ prāha vihagānām adhīśvaram
namaskartum athecchanti nāgāḥ svāmitvam āgatāḥ //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विनता स्वसुतं प्राह विहगानाम् अधीश्वरम्
नमस्कर्तुम् अथेच्छन्ति नागाः स्वामित्वम् आगताः ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Vinatā spoke to her son, the sovereign of birds: / “Now the serpents, having attained mastery, wish to pay homage

159.s:
bhāsvantam ity uvāceyaṃ māṃ sarpajananī haṭhāt
tathety uktvā sa garuḍo mām ārohantu pannagāḥ //
159.d:
भास्वन्तम् इत्य् उवाचेयं मां सर्पजननी हठात्
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा स गरुडो माम् आरोहन्तु पन्नगाः ॥
159.m: to the Shining One—so this mother of serpents has insisted to me.” / Saying “So be it,” Garuḍa said: “Let the serpents mount me.”

159.s:
tadārūḍhaṃ sarpasainyaṃ garuḍaṃ vihagādhipam
śanaiḥ śanair upagamad yatra devo divākaraḥ
te dahyamānās tīkṣṇena bhānutāpena vivyathuḥ //
159.d:
तदारूढं सर्पसैन्यं गरुडं विहगाधिपम्
शनैः शनैर् उपगमद् यत्र देवो दिवाकरः
ते दह्यमानास् तीक्ष्णेन भानुतापेन विव्यथुः ॥
159.m: Then the army of serpents, mounted upon Garuḍa, the lord of birds, / slowly approached the place where the divine sun was; / scorched by the fierce heat of the sun, they suffered agony.

159.s:
sarpā ūcuḥ
nivartasva mahāprājña pataṃgāya namo namaḥ
alaṃ sūryasya sadanaṃ dagdhāḥ sūryasya tejasā
yāmas tvayā vā garuḍa vihāya tvām athāpi vā //
159.d:
सर्पा ऊचुः
निवर्तस्व महाप्राज्ञ पतंगाय नमो नमः
अलं सूर्यस्य सदनं दग्धाः सूर्यस्य तेजसा
यामस् त्वया वा गरुड विहाय त्वाम् अथापि वा ॥
159.m: The serpents said: / 'Turn back, O great in wisdom; salutations again and again to the bird! / Enough of the abode of the sun; we are burnt by the brilliance of the sun! / We shall go with you, O Garuḍa, or even leaving you.'"

159.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ nāgair ucyamāna ādityaṃ darśayāmi vaḥ
ity uktvā gaganaṃ śīghraṃ jagāmādityasaṃmukhaḥ //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं नागैर् उच्यमान आदित्यं दर्शयामि वः
इत्य् उक्त्वा गगनं शीघ्रं जगामादित्यसंमुखः ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Spoken to in this manner by the serpents, he said, "I will show you the sun." / Having said this, he quickly went into the sky facing the sun.

159.s:
dagdhabhogā nipetus te dvīpaṃ taṃ vīraṇaṃ prati
bahavaḥ śatasāhasrāḥ pīḍitā dagdhavigrahāḥ //
159.d:
दग्धभोगा निपेतुस् ते द्वीपं तं वीरणं प्रति
बहवः शतसाहस्राः पीडिता दग्धविग्रहाः ॥
159.m: With their hoods burned, they fell down toward that Vīraṇa island, / many hundreds of thousands of them, tormented, their bodies scorched.

159.s:
putrāṇām ārtasaṃnādaṃ patitānāṃ mahītale
āśvāsituṃ samāyātā tān sā kadrūḥ suvihvalā //
159.d:
पुत्राणाम् आर्तसंनादं पतितानां महीतले
आश्वासितुं समायाता तान् सा कद्रूः सुविह्वला ॥
159.m: Hearing the cry of distress of her sons fallen upon the earth, / Kadrū came there deeply distraught to comfort them.

159.s:
uvāca vinatāṃ kadrūs tava putro 'tiduṣkṛtam
kṛtavān atidurmedhā yeṣāṃ śāntir na vidyate //
159.d:
उवाच विनतां कद्रूस् तव पुत्रो ऽतिदुष्कृतम्
कृतवान् अतिदुर्मेधा येषां शान्तिर् न विद्यते ॥
159.m: Kadrū said to Vinatā: "Your exceedingly foolish son / has committed a terrible wrong, for which there is no remedy.

159.s:
nānyathā kartum āyāti svāmivākyaṃ phaṇīśvaraḥ
sa kāśyapo bṛhattejā yady atra syād anāmayam //
159.d:
नान्यथा कर्तुम् आयाति स्वामिवाक्यं फणीश्वरः
स काश्यपो बृहत्तेजा यद्य् अत्र स्याद् अनामयम् ॥
159.m: The lord of serpents cannot transgress the word of his master. / If the mighty Kāśyapa were here, there would be relief.

159.s:
bhavec caivaṃ kathaṃ śāntiḥ putrāṇāṃ mama bhāmini
kadrvās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vinatā hy atibhītavat //
159.d:
भवेच् चैवं कथं शान्तिः पुत्राणां मम भामिनि
कद्र्वास् तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा विनता ह्य् अतिभीतवत् ॥
159.m: How then may relief come to my sons, fair lady?" / Hearing those words of Kadrū, Vinatā, as if terrified,

159.s: putram āha mahātmānaṃ garuḍaṃ vihagādhipam //
159.d: पुत्रम् आह महात्मानं गरुडं विहगाधिपम् ॥
159.m: spoke to her great-souled son, Garuḍa, the lord of birds.

159.s:
vinatovāca
nedaṃ yuktataraṃ putra bhūṣaṇaṃ vinayena hi
vartituṃ yuktam ity uktaṃ vaiparītyaṃ na yujyate //
159.d:
विनतोवाच
नेदं युक्ततरं पुत्र भूषणं विनयेन हि
वर्तितुं युक्तम् इत्य् उक्तं वैपरीत्यं न युज्यते ॥
159.m: Vinatā said: / "Son, this is not proper; modesty is indeed the true ornament. / It is said that one ought to behave appropriately; contrary behavior is unseemly.

159.s:
nāmitreṣv api kartavyaṃ sadbhir jihmaṃ kadācana
śrotriye cāntyaje vāpi samaṃ candraḥ prakāśate //
159.d:
नामित्रेष्व् अपि कर्तव्यं सद्भिर् जिह्मं कदाचन
श्रोत्रिये चान्त्यजे वापि समं चन्द्रः प्रकाशते ॥
159.m: Good people should never act crookedly, even toward enemies. / The moon shines equally upon a Vedic scholar or an outcaste.

159.s:
kurvanty aniṣṭaṃ kapaṭais ta eva mama putraka
prasahya kartuṃ ye sākṣād aśaktāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ //
159.d:
कुर्वन्त्य् अनिष्टं कपटैस् त एव मम पुत्रक
प्रसह्य कर्तुं ये साक्षाद् अशक्ताः पुरुषाधमाः ॥
159.m: My little son, it is only those basest of men / who, being unable to act openly by force, cause harm through deceit."

159.s:
brahmovāca
vinatā ca tataḥ prāha kadrūṃ tāṃ sarpamātaram //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विनता च ततः प्राह कद्रूं तां सर्पमातरम् ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / And then Vinatā said to Kadrū, that mother of serpents:

159.s:
vinatovāca
kiṃ kṛtvā śāntir abhyeti putrāṇāṃ te karomi tat
jarayā tu gṛhītās te vada śāntiṃ karomi tat //
159.d:
विनतोवाच
किं कृत्वा शान्तिर् अभ्येति पुत्राणां ते करोमि तत्
जरया तु गृहीतास् ते वद शान्तिं करोमि तत् ॥
159.m: Vinatā said: / "By doing what will relief come to your sons? I will do that. / They have been seized by decay; tell me the remedy, and I will perform it."

159.s:
brahmovāca
kadrūr apy āha vinatāṃ rasātalagataṃ payaḥ
tenābhiṣecitānāṃ me putrāṇāṃ śāntir eṣyati //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कद्रूर् अप्य् आह विनतां रसातलगतं पयः
तेनाभिषेचितानां मे पुत्राणां शान्तिर् एष्यति ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Kadrū in turn said to Vinatā: "The water that has reached the netherworld— / when sprinkled with that, relief will come to my sons."

159.s:
kadrvās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rasātalagataṃ payaḥ
kṣaṇenaiva samānīya nāgāṃs tān abhyaṣecayat
tataḥ provāca garuḍo maghavānaṃ śatakratum //
159.d:
कद्र्वास् तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा रसातलगतं पयः
क्षणेनैव समानीय नागांस् तान् अभ्यषेचयत्
ततः प्रोवाच गरुडो मघवानं शतक्रतुम् ॥
159.m: Hearing those words of Kadrū, he brought in an instant the water / that was in the netherworld, and sprinkled those serpents. / Then Garuḍa spoke to Maghavan, the performer of a hundred sacrifices:

159.s:
garuḍa uvāca
meghāś cāpy atra varṣantu trailokyasyopakāriṇaḥ //
159.d:
गरुड उवाच
मेघाश् चाप्य् अत्र वर्षन्तु त्रैलोक्यस्योपकारिणः ॥
159.m: Garuḍa said: / "Let the clouds, which benefit the three worlds, rain down here as well."

159.s:
brahmovāca
tathā vavarṣa parjanyo nāgānām abhavac chivam
rasātalabhavaṃ gāṅgaṃ nāgasaṃjīvanaṃ payaḥ //
159.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथा ववर्ष पर्जन्यो नागानाम् अभवच् छिवम्
रसातलभवं गाङ्गं नागसंजीवनं पयः ॥
159.m: Brahmā said: / Thereupon Parjanya rained, and good fortune came to the serpents. / The Gangetic water arising from the netherworld was the reviver of the serpents.

159.s:
jarāśokavināśārtham ānītaṃ garuḍena yat
yatrābhiṣecitā nāgās tan nāgālayam ucyate //
159.d:
जराशोकविनाशार्थम् आनीतं गरुडेन यत्
यत्राभिषेचिता नागास् तन् नागालयम् उच्यते ॥
159.m: Because it was brought by Garuḍa to destroy old age and sorrow, / the place where the serpents were sprinkled is called Nāgālaya.

159.s:
garuḍena yato vāri ānītaṃ tad rasātalāt
tad gāṅgaṃ vāri sarveṣāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
159.d:
गरुडेन यतो वारि आनीतं तद् रसातलात्
तद् गाङ्गं वारि सर्वेषां सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
159.m: Since that water was brought from the netherworld by Garuḍa, / that water of the Gaṅgā destroys all sins for everyone.

159.s:
jarāyā vāraṇaṃ yasmān nāgānām abhavac chivam
rasātalabhavaṃ gāṅgaṃ nāgasaṃjīvanaṃ yataḥ //
159.d:
जराया वारणं यस्मान् नागानाम् अभवच् छिवम्
रसातलभवं गाङ्गं नागसंजीवनं यतः ॥
159.m: Since there was the warding off of old age and good fortune for the serpents, / and because the Gangetic water arising from the netherworld revived the serpents,

159.s:
jarāśokavināśārthaṃ gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe
sākṣād amṛtasaṃvāhā vañjarā sābhavan nadī //
159.d:
जराशोकविनाशार्थं गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे
साक्षाद् अमृतसंवाहा वञ्जरा साभवन् नदी ॥
159.m: for the destruction of old age and sorrow, on the southern bank of the Gaṅgā / that river Vañjarā came into being, truly carrying ambrosia.

159.s:
jarādāridryasaṃtāpahāriṇī kleśavāriṇī
rasātalabhavā gaṅgā martyalokabhavā tu yā //
159.d:
जरादारिद्र्यसंतापहारिणी क्लेशवारिणी
रसातलभवा गङ्गा मर्त्यलोकभवा तु या ॥
159.m: Removing old age, poverty, and torment, and averting distress, / the Gaṅgā born of the netherworld and the one born in the mortal realm—

159.s:
tayoś ca saṃgamo yaḥ syāt kiṃ punas tatra varṇyate
yasyānusmaraṇād eva nāśaṃ yānty aghasaṃcayāḥ //
159.d:
तयोश् च संगमो यः स्यात् किं पुनस् तत्र वर्ण्यते
यस्यानुस्मरणाद् एव नाशं यान्त्य् अघसंचयाः ॥
159.m: what more can be said of the confluence of these two, / by the mere remembrance of which heaps of sin perish?

159.s:
tatra ca snānadānānāṃ phalaṃ ko vaktum īśvaraḥ
sapādaṃ tatra tīrthānāṃ lakṣam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ //
159.d:
तत्र च स्नानदानानां फलं को वक्तुम् ईश्वरः
सपादं तत्र तीर्थानां लक्षम् आहुर् मनीषिणः ॥
159.m: Who is capable of describing the fruit of bathing and gift-giving there? / Wise men declare there are one hundred and twenty-five thousand sacred places there.

159.s:
sarvasaṃpattidātṝṇāṃ sarvapāpaughahāriṇām
vañjarāsaṃgamasamaṃ tīrthaṃ kvāpi na vidyate
yadanusmaraṇenāpi vipadyante vipattayaḥ //
159.d:
सर्वसंपत्तिदातॄणां सर्वपापौघहारिणाम्
वञ्जरासंगमसमं तीर्थं क्वापि न विद्यते
यदनुस्मरणेनापि विपद्यन्ते विपत्तयः ॥
159.m: Bestowing all prosperity, removing the flood of all sins, / there is nowhere a sacred place equal to the confluence of the Vañjarā, / by the mere remembrance of which misfortunes perish.

160.s:
brahmovāca
devāgamaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ śivam
bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṝṇāṃ pitṝṇāṃ tṛptikārakam //
160.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
देवागमं नाम तीर्थं सर्वकामप्रदं शिवम्
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नॄणां पितॄणां तृप्तिकारकम् ॥
160.m: Brahmā said: / The sacred place named Devāgama grants all desires, is auspicious, / bestows enjoyment and liberation to men, and brings satisfaction to the ancestors.

160.s:
tatra vṛttaṃ samākhyāsye tava yatnena nārada
devānām asurāṇāṃ ca spardhābhūd dhanahetave //
160.d:
तत्र वृत्तं समाख्यास्ये तव यत्नेन नारद
देवानाम् असुराणां च स्पर्धाभूद् धनहेतवे ॥
160.m: I shall relate to you with care what happened there, Nārada. / A rivalry arose between the gods and the asuras over wealth.

160.s:
svargaḥ surāṇām abhavad asurāṇām ilābhavat
karmabhūmim avaṣṭabhya asurāḥ sarvato 'bhavan //
160.d:
स्वर्गः सुराणाम् अभवद् असुराणाम् इलाभवत्
कर्मभूमिम् अवष्टभ्य असुराः सर्वतो ऽभवन् ॥
160.m: Heaven belonged to the gods, and the earth belonged to the asuras. / Taking possession of the land of action, the asuras spread everywhere.

160.s:
devānāṃ yajñabhāgāṃś ca dātṝn ghnanty asurās tataḥ
tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve yajñabhāgair vinā kṛtāḥ //
160.d:
देवानां यज्ञभागांश् च दातॄन् घ्नन्त्य् असुरास् ततः
ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे यज्ञभागैर् विना कृताः ॥
160.m: Then the asuras killed the donors and seized the sacrificial shares of the gods. / Thereupon all the hosts of gods were deprived of their sacrificial shares.

160.s:
vyathitā mām upājagmuḥ kiṃ kṛtyam iti cābruvan
mayā coktāḥ suragaṇā yuddhe jitvāsurān balāt //
160.d:
व्यथिता माम् उपाजग्मुः किं कृत्यम् इति चाब्रुवन्
मया चोक्ताः सुरगणा युद्धे जित्वासुरान् बलात् ॥
160.m: Afflicted, they came to me and said, "What is to be done?" / And I told the hosts of gods: "Conquering the asuras by force in battle,

160.s:
bhuvaṃ prāpsyatha karmāṇi havīṃṣi ca yaśāṃsi ca
tathety uktvā gatā devā bhūmiṃ te samarārthinaḥ //
160.d:
भुवं प्राप्स्यथ कर्माणि हवींषि च यशांसि च
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा गता देवा भूमिं ते समरार्थिनः ॥
160.m: you will regain the earth, rituals, oblations, and renown." / Saying "So be it," the gods went to the earth, eager for battle.

160.s:
daityāś ca dānavāś caiva rākṣasā baladarpitāḥ
ekībhūtvā yayus te 'pi jayino yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ //
160.d:
दैत्याश् च दानवाश् चैव राक्षसा बलदर्पिताः
एकीभूत्वा ययुस् ते ऽपि जयिनो युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
160.m: And the daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas, proud of their strength, / united and also went forth, desiring victory and battle:

160.s:
ahir vṛtro balis tvāṣṭrir namuciḥ śambaro mayaḥ
ete cānye ca bahavo yoddhāro baladarpitāḥ //
160.d:
अहिर् वृत्रो बलिस् त्वाष्ट्रिर् नमुचिः शम्बरो मयः
एते चान्ये च बहवो योद्धारो बलदर्पिताः ॥
160.m: Ahi, Vṛtra, Bali, Tvāṣṭra, Namuci, Śambara, Maya, / these and many other warriors proud of their strength;

160.s:
agnir indro 'tha varuṇas tvaṣṭā pūṣā tathāśvinau
maruto lokapālāś ca nānāyuddhaviśāradāḥ //
160.d:
अग्निर् इन्द्रो ऽथ वरुणस् त्वष्टा पूषा तथाश्विनौ
मरुतो लोकपालाश् च नानायुद्धविशारदाः ॥
160.m: Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan, and the Aśvins, / the Maruts and the world-protectors, skilled in various types of combat.

160.s:
te dānavāḥ sarva eva yāmyāṃ vai diśi saṃgare
akurvanta mahāyatnaṃ dakṣiṇārṇavasaṃsthitāḥ //
160.d:
ते दानवाः सर्व एव याम्यां वै दिशि संगरे
अकुर्वन्त महायत्नं दक्षिणार्णवसंस्थिताः ॥
160.m: All those dānavas, stationed by the southern ocean, / made a great effort in battle in the southern direction.

160.s:
trikūṭaḥ parvataśreṣṭho rākṣasānāṃ purābhavat
tadvanena yayuḥ sarve taiḥ sārdhaṃ dakṣiṇārṇavam //
160.d:
त्रिकूटः पर्वतश्रेष्ठो राक्षसानां पुराभवत्
तद्वनेन ययुः सर्वे तैः सार्धं दक्षिणार्णवम् ॥
160.m: Trikūṭa, the foremost of mountains, had formerly belonged to the rākṣasas; / through its forest they all went together with them to the southern ocean.

160.s:
sarveṣāṃ melanaṃ yatra parvato malayas tu saḥ
malayasyāpi deśo 'sau devārīṇām abhūt tadā //
160.d:
सर्वेषां मेलनं यत्र पर्वतो मलयस् तु सः
मलयस्यापि देशो ऽसौ देवारीणाम् अभूत् तदा ॥
160.m: The mountain where the assembly of them all took place was Malaya; / that region of Malaya belonged at that time to the enemies of the gods.

160.s:
devānāṃ gautamītīre tatra saṃnihitaḥ śivaḥ
iti teṣāṃ samāyogo devānām abhavat kila //
160.d:
देवानां गौतमीतीरे तत्र संनिहितः शिवः
इति तेषां समायोगो देवानाम् अभवत् किल ॥
160.m: Śiva was present there for the gods on the bank of the Gautamī; / thus indeed occurred the assembly of those gods.

160.s:
devāḥ svaratham ārūḍhās tatra tatra samāgaman
gautamyāḥ saridambāyāḥ puline vimalāśayāḥ //
160.d:
देवाः स्वरथम् आरूढास् तत्र तत्र समागमन्
गौतम्याः सरिदम्बायाः पुलिने विमलाशयाः ॥
160.m: Mounted on their chariots, pure-minded, the gods assembled / in various places on the sandbank of the Gautamī, the mother of rivers,

160.s:
prasannābhīṣṭadā yā syāt pitṝṇām akhilasya tu
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve stutvā devaṃ maheśvaram
abhayaṃ cintayām āsus te sarve 'tha parasparam //
160.d:
प्रसन्नाभीष्टदा या स्यात् पितॄणाम् अखिलस्य तु
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे स्तुत्वा देवं महेश्वरम्
अभयं चिन्तयाम् आसुस् ते सर्वे ऽथ परस्परम् ॥
160.m: who is gracious and grants desires to the ancestors and to everyone. / Then all the hosts of gods, having praised the lord Maheśvara, / deliberated among themselves for safety.

160.s:
devā ūcuḥ
atrāpy upāyaḥ ko 'smākaṃ nirjitānāṃ parair haṭhāt
ekam evātra naḥ śreyo vijayo vāthavā mṛtiḥ
sapatnair abhibhūtānāṃ jīvitaṃ dhiṅ manasvinām //
160.d:
देवा ऊचुः
अत्राप्य् उपायः को ऽस्माकं निर्जितानां परैर् हठात्
एकम् एवात्र नः श्रेयो विजयो वाथवा मृतिः
सपत्नैर् अभिभूतानां जीवितं धिङ् मनस्विनाम् ॥
160.m: The gods said: / "What is our recourse here, forcibly defeated by the enemies? / Only one thing is our best good here: victory or else death. / Fie on the life of proud beings who are overcome by rivals!"

160.s:
brahmovāca
etasminn antare putra vāg uvācāśarīriṇī //
160.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे पुत्र वाग् उवाचाशरीरिणी ॥
160.m: Brahmā said: / In the meantime, my son, a bodiless voice spoke.

160.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
kleśenālaṃ suragaṇā gautamīm āśu gacchata
bhaktyā hariharau tatra samārādhayateśvarau //
160.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
क्लेशेनालं सुरगणा गौतमीम् आशु गच्छत
भक्त्या हरिहरौ तत्र समाराधयतेश्वरौ ॥
160.m: The voice from the sky said: / "Cease your distress, hosts of gods! Go quickly to the Gautamī; / worship there with devotion the two lords, Hari and Hara.

160.s: godāvaryās tayoś caiva prasādāt kiṃ tu duṣkaram //
160.d: गोदावर्यास् तयोश् चैव प्रसादात् किं तु दुष्करम् ॥
160.m: Through the grace of the Godāvarī and of those two, what is difficult?"

160.s:
brahmovāca
prasannābhyāṃ harīśābhyāṃ devā jayam abhīpsitam
avāpya sarvato jagmuḥ pālayanto divaukasaḥ //
160.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
प्रसन्नाभ्यां हरीशाभ्यां देवा जयम् अभीप्सितम्
अवाप्य सर्वतो जग्मुः पालयन्तो दिवौकसः ॥
160.m: Brahmā said: / When Hari and the Lord were pleased, the gods obtained their desired victory; / the dwellers of heaven went in every direction, protecting [the realms].

160.s:
yatra devāgamo jātas tat tīrthaṃ tena viśrutam
devāgamaṃ praśaṃsanti munayas tattvadarśinaḥ //
160.d:
यत्र देवागमो जातस् तत् तीर्थं तेन विश्रुतम्
देवागमं प्रशंसन्ति मुनयस् तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
160.m: Where the arrival of the gods took place, that sacred place is renowned by that name. / The sages who see reality praise Devāgama.

160.s:
tatrāśītisahasrāṇi śivaliṅgāni nārada
devāgamaḥ parvato 'sau priya ity api kathyate
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ devapriyam ato viduḥ //
160.d:
तत्राशीतिसहस्राणि शिवलिङ्गानि नारद
देवागमः पर्वतो ऽसौ प्रिय इत्य् अपि कथ्यते
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं देवप्रियम् अतो विदुः ॥
160.m: There are eighty thousand liṅgas of Śiva there, Nārada. / That mountain Devāgama is also called Priya; / hence from that time forth they know that sacred place as Devapriya.

161.s:
brahmovāca
kuśatarpaṇam ākhyātaṃ praṇītāsaṃgamaṃ tathā
tīrthaṃ sarveṣu lokeṣu bhuktimuktipradāyakam //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कुशतर्पणम् आख्यातं प्रणीतासंगमं तथा
तीर्थं सर्वेषु लोकेषु भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकम् ॥
161.m: Brahmā said: / Kuśatarpaṇa has thus been described, and likewise the confluence of the Praṇītā, / a sacred place that bestows enjoyment and liberation in all worlds.

161.s:
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu pāpaharaṃ śubham
vindhyasya dakṣiṇe pārśve sahyo nāma mahāgiriḥ //
161.d:
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि शृणु पापहरं शुभम्
विन्ध्यस्य दक्षिणे पार्श्वे सह्यो नाम महागिरिः ॥
161.m: I shall describe its true nature; listen to that auspicious [account] which removes sins: / On the southern side of the Vindhya, there is a great mountain named Sahya,

161.s:
yadaṅghribhyo 'bhavan nadyo godābhīmarathīmukhāḥ
yatrābhavat tad virajam ekavīrā ca yatra sā //
161.d:
यदङ्घ्रिभ्यो ऽभवन् नद्यो गोदाभीमरथीमुखाः
यत्राभवत् तद् विरजम् एकवीरा च यत्र सा ॥
161.m: from whose feet arose rivers headed by the Godā and Bhīmarathī; / where Viraja came into being, and where that Ekavīrā [is].

161.s:
na tasya mahimā kaiścid api śakyo 'nuvarṇitum
tasmin girau puṇyadeśe śṛṇu nārada yatnataḥ //
161.d:
न तस्य महिमा कैश्चिद् अपि शक्यो ऽनुवर्णितुम्
तस्मिन् गिरौ पुण्यदेशे शृणु नारद यत्नतः ॥
161.m: Its greatness cannot be described by anyone at all. / On that mountain, in that holy place, listen attentively, O Nārada.

161.s:
guhyād guhyataraṃ vakṣye sākṣād vedoditaṃ śubham
yan na jānanti munayo devāś ca pitaro 'surāḥ //
161.d:
गुह्याद् गुह्यतरं वक्ष्ये साक्षाद् वेदोदितं शुभम्
यन् न जानन्ति मुनयो देवाश् च पितरो ऽसुराः ॥
161.m: I shall declare what is more secret than the secret, auspicious, proclaimed directly by the Veda, / which sages, gods, ancestors, and asuras do not know.

161.s:
tad ahaṃ prītaye vakṣye śravaṇāt sarvakāmadam
paraḥ sa puruṣo jñeyo hy avyakto 'kṣara eva tu //
161.d:
तद् अहं प्रीतये वक्ष्ये श्रवणात् सर्वकामदम्
परः स पुरुषो ज्ञेयो ह्य् अव्यक्तो ऽक्षर एव तु ॥
161.m: I shall declare that for [your] delight, which grants all desires upon hearing: / That supreme puruṣa is to be known as unmanifest and imperishable indeed.

161.s:
aparaś ca kṣaras tasmāt prakṛtyanvita eva ca
nirākārāt sāvayavaḥ puruṣaḥ samajāyata //
161.d:
अपरश् च क्षरस् तस्मात् प्रकृत्यन्वित एव च
निराकारात् सावयवः पुरुषः समजायत ॥
161.m: And the other is perishable, proceeding from him and endowed with material nature. / From the formless, a puruṣa with limbs came into being.

161.s:
tasmād āpaḥ samudbhūtā adbhyaś ca puruṣas tathā
tābhyām abjaṃ samudbhūtaṃ tatrāham abhavaṃ mune //
161.d:
तस्माद् आपः समुद्भूता अद्भ्यश् च पुरुषस् तथा
ताभ्याम् अब्जं समुद्भूतं तत्राहम् अभवं मुने ॥
161.m: From him the waters were born, and from the waters the puruṣa; / from both of them the lotus was born, and there I arose, O sage.

161.s:
pṛthivī vāyur ākāśa āpo jyotis tathaiva ca
ete mattaḥ pūrvatarā ekadaivābhavan mune //
161.d:
पृथिवी वायुर् आकाश आपो ज्योतिस् तथैव च
एते मत्तः पूर्वतरा एकदैवाभवन् मुने ॥
161.m: Earth, wind, space, waters, and light— / these, earlier than I, arose all at once, O sage.

161.s:
etān eva prapaśyāmi nānyat sthāvarajaṅgamam
naiva vedās tadā cāsan nāhaṃ draṣṭāsmi kiṃcana //
161.d:
एतान् एव प्रपश्यामि नान्यत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्
नैव वेदास् तदा चासन् नाहं द्रष्टास्मि किंचन ॥
161.m: I beheld only these, nothing else, whether stationary or moving. / At that time the Vedas did not exist, nor did I see anything else.

161.s:
yasmād ahaṃ samudbhūto na paśyeyaṃ tam apy atha
tūṣṇīṃ sthite mayi tadā aśrauṣaṃ vācam uttamām //
161.d:
यस्माद् अहं समुद्भूतो न पश्येयं तम् अप्य् अथ
तूष्णीं स्थिते मयि तदा अश्रौषं वाचम् उत्तमाम् ॥
161.m: And I could not see him from whom I had arisen. / When I was standing silent then, I heard an exalted voice.

161.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
brahman kuru jagatsṛṣṭiṃ sthāvarasya carasya ca //
161.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
ब्रह्मन् कुरु जगत्सृष्टिं स्थावरस्य चरस्य च ॥
161.m:
The voice from the sky said:
O Brahmā, bring about the creation of the world, of the stationary and the moving.

161.s:
brahmovāca
tato 'ham abravaṃ vācaṃ paruṣāṃ tatra nārada
kathaṃ srakṣye kva vā srakṣye kena srakṣya idaṃ jagat //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो ऽहम् अब्रवं वाचं परुषां तत्र नारद
कथं स्रक्ष्ये क्व वा स्रक्ष्ये केन स्रक्ष्य इदं जगत् ॥
161.m:
Brahmā said:
Then I uttered a harsh voice there, O Nārada: / 'How shall I create? Where shall I create? With what shall I create this world?'

161.s:
saiva vāg abravīd daivī prakṛtir yābhidhīyate
viṣṇunā preritā mātā jagadīśā jaganmayī //
161.d:
सैव वाग् अब्रवीद् दैवी प्रकृतिर् याभिधीयते
विष्णुना प्रेरिता माता जगदीशा जगन्मयी ॥
161.m: That same divine voice, who is called material nature, / impelled by Viṣṇu, the mother, sovereign of the world, consisting of the universe, spoke.

161.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
yajñaṃ kuru tataḥ śaktis te bhavitrī na saṃśayaḥ
yajño vai viṣṇur ity eṣā śrutir brahman sanātanī //
161.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
यज्ञं कुरु ततः शक्तिस् ते भवित्री न संशयः
यज्ञो वै विष्णुर् इत्य् एषा श्रुतिर् ब्रह्मन् सनातनी ॥
161.m:
The voice from the sky said:
Perform a sacrifice; then power will come to you, without doubt. / 'Sacrifice is indeed Viṣṇu'—this is the eternal revelation, O Brahmā.

161.s: kiṃ yajvanām asādhyaṃ syād iha loke paratra ca //
161.d: किं यज्वनाम् असाध्यं स्याद् इह लोके परत्र च ॥
161.m: What could be unattainable for sacrificers in this world and in the next?

161.s:
brahmovāca
punas tām abravaṃ devīṃ kva vā keneti tad vada
yajñaḥ kāryo mahābhāge tataḥ sovāca māṃ prati //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुनस् ताम् अब्रवं देवीं क्व वा केनेति तद् वद
यज्ञः कार्यो महाभागे ततः सोवाच मां प्रति ॥
161.m:
Brahmā said:
Again I said to that goddess, 'Tell me where and with what / a sacrifice is to be performed, O fortunate one.' Then she spoke to me.

161.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
oṃkārabhūtā yā devī mātṛkalpā jaganmayī
karmabhūmau yajasveha yajñeśaṃ yajñapūruṣam //
161.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
ओंकारभूता या देवी मातृकल्पा जगन्मयी
कर्मभूमौ यजस्वेह यज्ञेशं यज्ञपूरुषम् ॥
161.m:
The voice from the sky said:
That goddess who has become the syllable Oṃ, mother-like, consisting of the world— / worship here on the land of action the lord of sacrifice, the Puruṣa of sacrifice.

161.s:
sa eva sādhanaṃ te syāt tena taṃ yaja suvrata
yajñaḥ svāhā svadhā mantrā brāhmaṇā havirādikam //
161.d:
स एव साधनं ते स्यात् तेन तं यज सुव्रत
यज्ञः स्वाहा स्वधा मन्त्रा ब्राह्मणा हविरादिकम् ॥
161.m: He alone shall be your means; with him worship him, O you of noble vows. / The sacrifice, svāhā, svadhā, the mantras, the brāhmaṇas, the oblation, and so forth—

161.s: harir evākhilaṃ tena sarvaṃ viṣṇor avāpyate //
161.d: हरिर् एवाखिलं तेन सर्वं विष्णोर् अवाप्यते ॥
161.m: Hari alone is everything; by him everything is obtained from Viṣṇu.

161.s:
brahmovāca
punas tām abravaṃ devīṃ karmabhūḥ kva vidhīyate
tadā nārada naivāsīd bhāgīrathy atha narmadā //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुनस् ताम् अब्रवं देवीं कर्मभूः क्व विधीयते
तदा नारद नैवासीद् भागीरथ्य् अथ नर्मदा ॥
161.m:
Brahmā said:
Again I said to that goddess: 'Where is the land of action ordained?' / At that time, O Nārada, there was no Bhāgīrathī, nor Narmadā,

161.s:
yamunā naiva tāpī sā sarasvaty atha gautamī
samudro vā nadaḥ kaścin na saraḥ sarito 'malāḥ
sā śaktiḥ punar apy evaṃ mām uvāca punaḥ punaḥ //
161.d:
यमुना नैव तापी सा सरस्वत्य् अथ गौतमी
समुद्रो वा नदः कश्चिन् न सरः सरितो ऽमलाः
सा शक्तिः पुनर् अप्य् एवं माम् उवाच पुनः पुनः ॥
161.m: nor Yamunā, nor that Tāpī, nor Sarasvatī, nor Gautamī, / nor ocean, nor any river, nor lake, nor clear streams. / That power spoke to me thus again and again.

161.s:
daivī vāg uvāca
sumeror dakṣiṇe pārśve tathā himavato gireḥ
dakṣiṇe cāpi vindhyasya sahyāc caivātha dakṣiṇe
sarvasya sarvakāle tu karmabhūmiḥ śubhodayā //
161.d:
दैवी वाग् उवाच
सुमेरोर् दक्षिणे पार्श्वे तथा हिमवतो गिरेः
दक्षिणे चापि विन्ध्यस्य सह्याच् चैवाथ दक्षिणे
सर्वस्य सर्वकाले तु कर्मभूमिः शुभोदया ॥
161.m:
The divine voice said:
On the southern side of Sumeru and of the Himavat mountain, / and south of the Vindhya, and south of the Sahya, / is the land of action of auspicious rise for everyone at all times.

161.s:
brahmovāca
tat tu vākyam atho śrutvā tyaktvā meruṃ mahāgirim
taṃ pradeśam athāgatya sthātavyaṃ kvety acintayam
tato mām abravīt saiva viṣṇor vāṇy aśarīriṇī //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तत् तु वाक्यम् अथो श्रुत्वा त्यक्त्वा मेरुं महागिरिम्
तं प्रदेशम् अथागत्य स्थातव्यं क्वेत्य् अचिन्तयम्
ततो माम् अब्रवीत् सैव विष्णोर् वाण्य् अशरीरिणी ॥
161.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard that speech, leaving the great mountain Meru / and having reached that region, I thought: 'Where am I to stay?' / Then that very bodiless voice of Viṣṇu spoke to me.

161.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
ito gaccha itas tiṣṭha tathopaviśa cātra hi
saṃkalpaṃ kuru yajñasya sa te yajñaḥ samāpyate //
161.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
इतो गच्छ इतस् तिष्ठ तथोपविश चात्र हि
संकल्पं कुरु यज्ञस्य स ते यज्ञः समाप्यते ॥
161.m:
The voice from the sky said:
Go this way; stay here, and indeed sit down here. / Form the intention for the sacrifice; that sacrifice of yours will be accomplished.

161.s:
kṛte caivātha saṃkalpe yajñārthe surasattama
yad vadanty akhilā vedā vidhe tat tat samācara //
161.d:
कृते चैवाथ संकल्पे यज्ञार्थे सुरसत्तम
यद् वदन्त्य् अखिला वेदा विधे तत् तत् समाचर ॥
161.m: And once the intention is formed for the sacrifice, O best of the gods, / perform whatever all the Vedas declare, O ordainer.

161.s:
brahmovāca
itihāsapurāṇāni yad anyac chabdagocaram
svato mukhe mama prāyād abhūc ca smṛtigocaram //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इतिहासपुराणानि यद् अन्यच् छब्दगोचरम्
स्वतो मुखे मम प्रायाद् अभूच् च स्मृतिगोचरम् ॥
161.m:
Brahmā said:
The epic histories, Purāṇas, and whatever else falls within the realm of sound / spontaneously came forth in my mouth and became the object of recollection.

161.s:
vedārthaś ca mayā sarvo jñāto 'sau tatkṣaṇena ca
tataḥ puruṣasūktaṃ tad asmaraṃ lokaviśrutam //
161.d:
वेदार्थश् च मया सर्वो ज्ञातो ऽसौ तत्क्षणेन च
ततः पुरुषसूक्तं तद् अस्मरं लोकविश्रुतम् ॥
161.m: And the entire meaning of the Veda was known by me in that very moment. / Then I remembered that world-renowned Puruṣasūkta.

161.s:
yajñopakaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ tad uktaṃ ca tv akalpayam
taduktena prakāreṇa yajñapātrāṇy akalpayam //
161.d:
यज्ञोपकरणं सर्वं तद् उक्तं च त्व् अकल्पयम्
तदुक्तेन प्रकारेण यज्ञपात्राण्य् अकल्पयम् ॥
161.m: And I prepared all the sacrificial implements declared in it; / in the manner spoken by it, I fashioned the sacrificial vessels.

161.s:
ahaṃ sthitvā yatra deśe śucir bhūtvā yatātmavān
dīkṣito vipradeśo 'sau mannāmnā tu prakīrtitaḥ //
161.d:
अहं स्थित्वा यत्र देशे शुचिर् भूत्वा यतात्मवान्
दीक्षितो विप्रदेशो ऽसौ मन्नाम्ना तु प्रकीर्तितः ॥
161.m: The region where I stayed, having become pure, self-restrained, / and initiated, is celebrated by my name.

161.s:
maddevayajanaṃ puṇyaṃ nāmnā brahmagiriḥ smṛtaḥ
caturaśītiparyantaṃ yojanāni mahāmune //
161.d:
मद्देवयजनं पुण्यं नाम्ना ब्रह्मगिरिः स्मृतः
चतुरशीतिपर्यन्तं योजनानि महामुने ॥
161.m: My holy place of divine worship is known by name as Brahmagiri, / extending for eighty-four yojanas, O great sage.

161.s:
maddevayajanaṃ puṇyaṃ pūrvato brahmaṇo gireḥ
tatra madhye vedikā syād gārhapatyo 'sya dakṣiṇe //
161.d:
मद्देवयजनं पुण्यं पूर्वतो ब्रह्मणो गिरेः
तत्र मध्ये वेदिका स्याद् गार्हपत्यो ऽस्य दक्षिणे ॥
161.m: My holy place of divine worship is to the east of Brahmā's mountain; / in the middle of it should be the altar, and the gārhapatya fire on its south.

161.s:
tatra cāhavanīyasya evam agnīṃs tv akalpayam
vinā patnyā na sidhyeta yajñaḥ śrutinidarśanāt //
161.d:
तत्र चाहवनीयस्य एवम् अग्नींस् त्व् अकल्पयम्
विना पत्न्या न सिध्येत यज्ञः श्रुतिनिदर्शनात् ॥
161.m: And there was the āhavanīya fire; thus I arranged the fires. / Without a wife a sacrifice cannot succeed, according to the teaching of the revelation.

161.s:
śarīram ātmano 'haṃ vai dvedhā cākaravaṃ mune
pūrvārdhena tataḥ patnī mamābhūd yajñasiddhaye //
161.d:
शरीरम् आत्मनो ऽहं वै द्वेधा चाकरवं मुने
पूर्वार्धेन ततः पत्नी ममाभूद् यज्ञसिद्धये ॥
161.m: I divided my own body into two, O sage; / from the front half my wife arose, for the accomplishment of the sacrifice,

161.s:
uttareṇa tv ahaṃ tadvad ardho jāyā iti śruteḥ
kālaṃ vasantam utkṛṣṭam ājyarūpeṇa nārada //
161.d:
उत्तरेण त्व् अहं तद्वद् अर्धो जाया इति श्रुतेः
कालं वसन्तम् उत्कृष्टम् आज्यरूपेण नारद ॥
161.m: and by the other half I was [myself], according to the Vedic text, 'The wife is half [the self].' / [I arranged] the excellent spring season in the form of clarified butter, O Nārada;

161.s:
akalpayaṃ tathā cedhmaṃ grīṣmaṃ cāpi śarad dhaviḥ
ṛtuṃ ca prāvṛṣaṃ putra tadā barhir akalpayam //
161.d:
अकल्पयं तथा चेध्मं ग्रीष्मं चापि शरद् धविः
ऋतुं च प्रावृषं पुत्र तदा बर्हिर् अकल्पयम् ॥
161.m: I arranged the summer as kindling wood, and autumn as the oblation; / and the rainy season, my son, I then arranged as the sacrificial grass.

161.s:
chandāṃsi sapta vai tatra tadā paridhayo 'bhavan
kalākāṣṭhānimeṣā hi samitpātrakuśāḥ smṛtāḥ //
161.d:
छन्दांसि सप्त वै तत्र तदा परिधयो ऽभवन्
कलाकाष्ठानिमेषा हि समित्पात्रकुशाः स्मृताः ॥
161.m: The seven metres then became the enclosing sticks; / the kalās, kāṣṭhās, and nimeṣas were known as the fuel, the vessel, and the kuśa grass.

161.s:
yo 'nādiś ca tv anantaś ca svayaṃ kālo 'bhavat tadā
yūparūpeṇa devarṣe yoktraṃ ca paśubandhanam //
161.d:
यो ऽनादिश् च त्व् अनन्तश् च स्वयं कालो ऽभवत् तदा
यूपरूपेण देवर्षे योक्त्रं च पशुबन्धनम् ॥
161.m: Time itself, which is beginningless and endless, then became / the sacrificial post, O divine sage, and the halter for tying the beast.

161.s:
sattvāditriguṇāḥ pāśā naiva tatrābhavat paśuḥ
tato 'ham abravaṃ vācaṃ vaiṣṇavīm aśarīriṇīm //
161.d:
सत्त्वादित्रिगुणाः पाशा नैव तत्राभवत् पशुः
ततो ऽहम् अब्रवं वाचं वैष्णवीम् अशरीरिणीम् ॥
161.m: The three qualities, beginning with sattva, were the bonds; but there was no sacrificial beast there at all. / Then I addressed the bodiless Vaiṣṇava voice:

161.s:
vinaiva paśunā nāyaṃ yajñaḥ parisamāpyate
tato mām avadad devī saiva nityāśarīriṇī //
161.d:
विनैव पशुना नायं यज्ञः परिसमाप्यते
ततो माम् अवदद् देवी सैव नित्याशरीरिणी ॥
161.m: 'Without a beast this sacrifice cannot be completed.' / Then that very goddess, eternally bodiless, spoke to me.

161.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
pauruṣeṇātha sūktena stuhi taṃ puruṣaṃ param //
161.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
पौरुषेणाथ सूक्तेन स्तुहि तं पुरुषं परम् ॥
161.m:
The voice from the sky said:
Praise that supreme puruṣa with the Puruṣasūkta.

161.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā stūyamāne devadeve janārdane
mama cotpādake bhaktyā sūktena puruṣasya hi //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा स्तूयमाने देवदेवे जनार्दने
मम चोत्पादके भक्त्या सूक्तेन पुरुषस्य हि ॥
161.m:
Brahmā said:
Saying 'So be it,' when the god of gods, Janārdana, / my creator, was being praised with devotion with the hymn of the Puruṣa,

161.s:
sā ca mām abravīd devī brahman māṃ tvaṃ paśuṃ kuru
tadā vijñāya puruṣaṃ janakaṃ mama cāvyayam //
161.d:
सा च माम् अब्रवीद् देवी ब्रह्मन् मां त्वं पशुं कुरु
तदा विज्ञाय पुरुषं जनकं मम चाव्ययम् ॥
161.m: that goddess said to me: 'O Brahmā, make me the sacrificial beast.' / Then, having understood the imperishable Puruṣa, my progenitor,

161.s:
kālayūpasya pārśve taṃ guṇapāśair niveśitam
barhisthitam ahaṃ praukṣaṃ puruṣaṃ jātam agrataḥ //
161.d:
कालयूपस्य पार्श्वे तं गुणपाशैर् निवेशितम्
बर्हिस्थितम् अहं प्रौक्षं पुरुषं जातम् अग्रतः ॥
161.m: placed beside the sacrificial post of time, bound with the cords of the qualities, / and standing upon the sacrificial grass, I sprinkled that Puruṣa born in the beginning.

161.s:
etasminn antare tatra tasmāt sarvam abhūd idam
brāhmaṇās tu mukhāt tasya 'bhavan bāhvoś ca kṣatriyāḥ //
161.d:
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र तस्मात् सर्वम् अभूद् इदम्
ब्राह्मणास् तु मुखात् तस्य ऽभवन् बाह्वोश् च क्षत्रियाः ॥
161.m: Meanwhile, right there, all this arose from him: / the brāhmaṇas arose from his mouth, and the kṣatriyas from his two arms;

161.s:
mukhād indras tathāgniś ca śvasanaḥ prāṇato 'bhavat
diśaḥ śrotrāt tathā śīrṣṇaḥ sarvaḥ svargo 'bhavat tadā //
161.d:
मुखाद् इन्द्रस् तथाग्निश् च श्वसनः प्राणतो ऽभवत्
दिशः श्रोत्रात् तथा शीर्ष्णः सर्वः स्वर्गो ऽभवत् तदा ॥
161.m: from his mouth arose Indra and Agni, and from his breath the wind; / from his ear the directions, and from his head all heaven then arose;

161.s:
manasaś candramā jātaḥ sūryo 'bhūc cakṣuṣas tathā
antarikṣaṃ tathā nābher ūrubhyāṃ viśa eva ca //
161.d:
मनसश् चन्द्रमा जातः सूर्यो ऽभूच् चक्षुषस् तथा
अन्तरिक्षं तथा नाभेर् ऊरुभ्यां विश एव च ॥
161.m: from his mind the moon was born, and from his eye the sun arose; / the atmosphere from his navel, and the vaiśyas from his thighs.

161.s:
padbhyāṃ śūdraś ca saṃjātas tathā bhūmir ajāyata
ṛṣayo romakūpebhya oṣadhyaḥ keśato 'bhavan //
161.d:
पद्भ्यां शूद्रश् च संजातस् तथा भूमिर् अजायत
ऋषयो रोमकूपेभ्य ओषध्यः केशतो ऽभवन् ॥
161.m: From the feet the śūdra was born, and the earth was born likewise; / from the pores of the skin the sages arose, and plants arose from the hair.

161.s:
grāmyāraṇyāś ca paśavo nakhebhyaḥ sarvato 'bhavan
kṛmikīṭapataṃgādi pāyūpasthād ajāyata //
161.d:
ग्राम्यारण्याश् च पशवो नखेभ्यः सर्वतो ऽभवन्
कृमिकीटपतंगादि पायूपस्थाद् अजायत ॥
161.m: Domestic and wild animals arose everywhere from the nails; / worms, insects, winged creatures, and the like arose from the anus and sexual organs.

161.s:
sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ kiṃcid dṛśyādṛśyaṃ ca kiṃcana
tasmāt sarvam abhūd devā mattaś cāpy abhavan punaḥ
etasminn antare saiva viṣṇor vāg abravīc ca mām //
161.d:
स्थावरं जङ्गमं किंचिद् दृश्यादृश्यं च किंचन
तस्मात् सर्वम् अभूद् देवा मत्तश् चाप्य् अभवन् पुनः
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे सैव विष्णोर् वाग् अब्रवीच् च माम् ॥
161.m: Whatever is stationary or moving, visible or invisible, / all arose from him, O gods, and arose again from me. / In the meantime, that very voice of Viṣṇu spoke to me:

161.s:
ākāśavāg uvāca
sarvaṃ saṃpūrṇam abhavat sṛṣṭir jātā tathepsitā
idānīṃ juhudhi hy agnau pātrāṇi ca samāni ca //
161.d:
आकाशवाग् उवाच
सर्वं संपूर्णम् अभवत् सृष्टिर् जाता तथेप्सिता
इदानीं जुहुधि ह्य् अग्नौ पात्राणि च समानि च ॥
161.m: The voice in the sky said: / 'Everything has become complete; the desired creation has taken place. / Now offer into the fire the vessels and the flat wooden ladles.

161.s:
visarjaya tathā yūpaṃ praṇītāṃ ca kuśāṃs tathā
ṛtvigrūpaṃ yajñarūpam uddeśyaṃ dhyeyam eva ca //
161.d:
विसर्जय तथा यूपं प्रणीतां च कुशांस् तथा
ऋत्विग्रूपं यज्ञरूपम् उद्देश्यं ध्येयम् एव च ॥
161.m: Dismiss likewise the sacrificial post, the holy water vessel, and the kuśa grasses, / the form of the priest, the form of the sacrifice, what is aimed at, and what is meditated upon;

161.s: sruvaṃ ca puruṣaṃ pāśān sarvaṃ brahman visarjaya //
161.d: स्रुवं च पुरुषं पाशान् सर्वं ब्रह्मन् विसर्जय ॥
161.m: the offering spoon, the cosmic person, the sacrificial cords—dismiss everything, O Brahmā!'

161.s:
brahmovāca
tadvākyasamakālaṃ tu kramaśo yajñayoniṣu
gārhapatye dakṣiṇāgnau tathā caiva mahāmune //
161.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद्वाक्यसमकालं तु क्रमशो यज्ञयोनिषु
गार्हपत्ये दक्षिणाग्नौ तथा चैव महामुने ॥
161.m: Brahmā said: / At the same time as those words, one after another into the sources of the sacrifice— / into the Gārhapatya, into the Dakṣiṇāgni, and likewise, O great sage,

161.s:
pūrvasminn api caivāgnau kramaśo juhvatas tadā
tatra tatra jagadyonim anusaṃdhāya pūruṣam //
161.d:
पूर्वस्मिन्न् अपि चैवाग्नौ क्रमशो जुह्वतस् तदा
तत्र तत्र जगद्योनिम् अनुसंधाय पूरुषम् ॥
161.m: and into the eastern fire as well, as I made offerings one after another at that time, / focusing my mind in each place upon the cosmic person, the origin of the world,

161.s:
mantrapūtaṃ śuciḥ samyag yajñadevo jaganmayaḥ
lokanātho viśvakartā kuṇḍānāṃ tatra saṃnidhau //
161.d:
मन्त्रपूतं शुचिः सम्यग् यज्ञदेवो जगन्मयः
लोकनाथो विश्वकर्ता कुण्डानां तत्र संनिधौ ॥
161.m: purified by mantras, clean, properly [meditating on] the lord of sacrifice who consists of the world, / the protector of the worlds, the creator of all, nearby the fire pits there:

161.s:
śuklarūpadharo viṣṇur bhaved āhavanīyake
śyāmo viṣṇur dakṣiṇāgneḥ pīto gṛhapateḥ kaveḥ //
161.d:
शुक्लरूपधरो विष्णुर् भवेद् आहवनीयके
श्यामो विष्णुर् दक्षिणाग्नेः पीतो गृहपतेः कवेः ॥
161.m: Viṣṇu, assuming a white form, is in the Āhavanīya; / Viṣṇu is dark in the Dakṣiṇāgni, and yellow in [the fire] of the master of the house, the wise one.

161.s:
sarvakālaṃ teṣu viṣṇur ato deśeṣu saṃsthitaḥ
na tena rahitaṃ kiṃcid viṣṇunā viśvayoninā //
161.d:
सर्वकालं तेषु विष्णुर् अतो देशेषु संस्थितः
न तेन रहितं किंचिद् विष्णुना विश्वयोनिना ॥
161.m: Therefore Viṣṇu remains at all times in those places; / there is nothing destitute of him, of Viṣṇu, the origin of all.

161.s:
praṇītāyāḥ praṇayanaṃ mantraiś cākaravaṃ tataḥ
praṇītodakam apy etat praṇīteti nadī śubhā //
161.d:
प्रणीतायाः प्रणयनं मन्त्रैश् चाकरवं ततः
प्रणीतोदकम् अप्य् एतत् प्रणीतेति नदी शुभा ॥
161.m: Then with mantras I carried out the fetching of the holy water vessel. / This holy water is itself the auspicious river named Praṇītā.

161.s:
vyasarjayaṃ praṇītāṃ tāṃ mārjayitvā kuśair atha
mārjane kriyamāṇe tu praṇītodakabindavaḥ //
161.d:
व्यसर्जयं प्रणीतां तां मार्जयित्वा कुशैर् अथ
मार्जने क्रियमाणे तु प्रणीतोदकबिन्दवः ॥
161.m: I dismissed that holy water vessel, having then sprinkled with kuśa grasses. / While the sprinkling was being performed, drops of holy water

161.s:
patitās tatra tīrthāni jātāni guṇavanti ca
saṃjātā muniśārdūla snānāt kratuphalapradā //
161.d:
पतितास् तत्र तीर्थानि जातानि गुणवन्ति च
संजाता मुनिशार्दूल स्नानात् क्रतुफलप्रदा ॥
161.m: fell, and there arose sacred bathing places endowed with virtues, / which arose, O tiger among sages, granting the fruit of sacrifices through bathing.

161.s:
yālaṃkṛtā sarvakālaṃ devadevena śārṅgiṇā
sopānapaṅktiḥ sarveṣāṃ vaikuṇṭhārohaṇāya sā //
161.d:
यालंकृता सर्वकालं देवदेवेन शार्ङ्गिणा
सोपानपङ्क्तिः सर्वेषां वैकुण्ठारोहणाय सा ॥
161.m: It is adorned at all times by the god of gods, the bearer of the Śārṅga bow; / it is a flight of stairs for everyone to ascend to Vaikuṇṭha.

161.s:
saṃmārjitāḥ kuśā yatra patitā bhūtale śubhe
kuśatarpaṇam ākhyātaṃ bahupuṇyaphalapradam //
161.d:
संमार्जिताः कुशा यत्र पतिता भूतले शुभे
कुशतर्पणम् आख्यातं बहुपुण्यफलप्रदम् ॥
161.m: Where the kuśa grasses used for sprinkling fell upon the auspicious ground, / that is celebrated as Kuśatarpaṇa, granting the reward of great merit.

161.s:
kuśaiś ca tarpitāḥ sarve kuśatarpaṇam ucyate
paścāc ca saṃgatā tatra gautamī kāraṇāntarāt //
161.d:
कुशैश् च तर्पिताः सर्वे कुशतर्पणम् उच्यते
पश्चाच् च संगता तत्र गौतमी कारणान्तरात् ॥
161.m: Because all were gratified with kuśa grasses, it is called Kuśatarpaṇa. / Afterwards, the Gautamī joined there for another reason.

161.s:
praṇītāyāṃ mahābuddhe praṇītāsaṃgamo 'bhavat
kuśatarpaṇadeśe tu tat tīrthaṃ kuśatarpaṇam //
161.d:
प्रणीतायां महाबुद्धे प्रणीतासंगमो ऽभवत्
कुशतर्पणदेशे तु तत् तीर्थं कुशतर्पणम् ॥
161.m: With the Praṇītā, O one of great intellect, occurred the confluence with the Praṇītā. / In the region of Kuśatarpaṇa, that sacred place is indeed Kuśatarpaṇa.

161.s:
tatraiva kalpito yūpo mayā vindhyasya cottare
visṛṣṭo lokapūjyo 'sau viṣṇor āsīt samāśrayaḥ //
161.d:
तत्रैव कल्पितो यूपो मया विन्ध्यस्य चोत्तरे
विसृष्टो लोकपूज्यो ऽसौ विष्णोर् आसीत् समाश्रयः ॥
161.m: Right there, north of the Vindhya, the sacrificial post was erected by me; / dismissed, worthy of worship by the worlds, it became a resting place for Viṣṇu.

161.s:
akṣayaś cābhavac chrīmān akṣayo 'sau vaṭo 'bhavat
nityaś ca kālarūpo 'sau smaraṇāt kratupuṇyadaḥ //
161.d:
अक्षयश् चाभवच् छ्रीमान् अक्षयो ऽसौ वटो ऽभवत्
नित्यश् च कालरूपो ऽसौ स्मरणात् क्रतुपुण्यदः ॥
161.m: It became imperishable and glorious; it became that imperishable banyan tree. / Eternal, possessing the form of time, it grants the merit of sacrifices by mere remembrance.

161.s:
maddevayajanaṃ cedaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyam ucyate
saṃpūrṇe tu kratau viṣṇur mayā bhaktyā prasāditaḥ //
161.d:
मद्देवयजनं चेदं दण्डकारण्यम् उच्यते
संपूर्णे तु क्रतौ विष्णुर् मया भक्त्या प्रसादितः ॥
161.m: This sacrificial ground of mine for the gods is called the Daṇḍaka Forest. / When the sacrifice was completed, Viṣṇu was propitiated by me with devotion.

161.s:
yo virāḍ ucyate vede yasmān mūrtam ajāyata
yasmāc ca mama cotpattir yasyedaṃ vikṛtaṃ jagat //
161.d:
यो विराड् उच्यते वेदे यस्मान् मूर्तम् अजायत
यस्माच् च मम चोत्पत्तिर् यस्येदं विकृतं जगत् ॥
161.m: He who is called Virāj in the Veda, from whom embodied form arose, / from whom my own origin [came], and whose transformed state this world is—

161.s:
tam ahaṃ devadeveśam abhivandya vyasarjayam
yojanāni caturviṃśan maddevayajanaṃ śubham //
161.d:
तम् अहं देवदेवेशम् अभिवन्द्य व्यसर्जयम्
योजनानि चतुर्विंशन् मद्देवयजनं शुभम् ॥
161.m: saluting that lord of the gods of gods, I dismissed him. / My auspicious sacrificial ground for the gods is twenty-four yojanas [wide].

161.s:
tasmād adyāpi kuṇḍāni santi ca trīṇi nārada
yajñeśvarasvarūpāṇi viṣṇor vai cakrapāṇinaḥ //
161.d:
तस्माद् अद्यापि कुण्डानि सन्ति च त्रीणि नारद
यज्ञेश्वरस्वरूपाणि विष्णोर् वै चक्रपाणिनः ॥
161.m: Therefore, even today there are three fire pits, O Nārada, / the embodiments of the lord of sacrifice, of Viṣṇu who holds the discus in his hand.

161.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti cākhyātaṃ maddevayajanaṃ ca tat
tatrasthaḥ kṛmikīṭādiḥ so 'py ante muktibhājanam //
161.d:
ततः प्रभृति चाख्यातं मद्देवयजनं च तत्
तत्रस्थः कृमिकीटादिः सो ऽप्य् अन्ते मुक्तिभाजनम् ॥
161.m: From then on, that place has been celebrated as my sacrificial ground for the gods; / worms, insects, and the like dwelling there also share in liberation at the end.

161.s:
dharmabījaṃ muktibījaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyam ucyate
viśeṣād gautamīśliṣṭo deśaḥ puṇyatamo 'bhavat //
161.d:
धर्मबीजं मुक्तिबीजं दण्डकारण्यम् उच्यते
विशेषाद् गौतमीश्लिष्टो देशः पुण्यतमो ऽभवत् ॥
161.m: The Daṇḍaka Forest is called the seed of dharma, the seed of liberation; / in particular, the region embraced by the Gautamī became most sacred.

161.s:
praṇītāsaṃgame cāpi kuśatarpaṇa eva vā
snānadānādi yaḥ kuryāt sa gacchet paramaṃ padam //
161.d:
प्रणीतासंगमे चापि कुशतर्पण एव वा
स्नानदानादि यः कुर्यात् स गच्छेत् परमं पदम् ॥
161.m: At the confluence with the Praṇītā or indeed at Kuśatarpaṇa, / whoever performs ablutions, gifts, and the like goes to the supreme abode.

161.s:
smaraṇaṃ paṭhanaṃ vāpi śravaṇaṃ cāpi bhaktitaḥ
sarvakāmapradaṃ puṃsāṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ viduḥ //
161.d:
स्मरणं पठनं वापि श्रवणं चापि भक्तितः
सर्वकामप्रदं पुंसां भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं विदुः ॥
161.m: Remembering, reciting, or hearing [about it] with devotion / is known to grant all desires to human beings, granting enjoyment and liberation.

161.s:
ubhayos tīrayos tatra tīrthāny āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi teṣu puṇyaṃ puroditam //
161.d:
उभयोस् तीरयोस् तत्र तीर्थान्य् आहुर् मनीषिणः
षडशीतिसहस्राणि तेषु पुण्यं पुरोदितम् ॥
161.m: The wise say there are sacred bathing places on both banks there, / eighty-six thousand in number; their merit has been declared previously.

161.s:
vārāṇasyā api mune kuśatarpaṇam uttamam
nānena sadṛśaṃ tīrthaṃ vidyate sacarācare //
161.d:
वाराणस्या अपि मुने कुशतर्पणम् उत्तमम्
नानेन सदृशं तीर्थं विद्यते सचराचरे ॥
161.m: Kuśatarpaṇa is superior even to Vārāṇasī, O sage; / no sacred bathing place equal to this exists among moving and unmoving beings.

161.s:
brahmahatyādipāpānāṃ smaraṇād api nāśanam
tīrtham etan mune proktaṃ svargadvāraṃ mahītale //
161.d:
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानां स्मरणाद् अपि नाशनम्
तीर्थम् एतन् मुने प्रोक्तं स्वर्गद्वारं महीतले ॥
161.m: It destroys sins such as brahmanicide merely through remembrance; / this sacred place, O sage, is declared to be the gate to heaven on the surface of the earth.

162.s:
brahmovāca
manyutīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam
sarvakāmapradaṃ nṝṇāṃ smaraṇād aghanāśanam //
162.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मन्युतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्
सर्वकामप्रदं नॄणां स्मरणाद् अघनाशनम् ॥
162.m: Brahmā said: / Celebrated as Manyutīrtha is that which completely destroys all sins, / granting all desires to men, destroying evils through remembrance.

162.s:
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvāvahito mune
devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca saṃgaro 'bhūn mithaḥ purā //
162.d:
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वावहितो मुने
देवानां दानवानां च संगरो ऽभून् मिथः पुरा ॥
162.m: I shall declare its power; listen attentively, O sage. / Formerly there was a battle between the gods and the Dānavas.

162.s:
tatrājayan naiva surā dānavā jayino 'bhavan
parāṅmukhāḥ suragaṇāḥ saṃgarād gatacetasaḥ //
162.d:
तत्राजयन् नैव सुरा दानवा जयिनो ऽभवन्
पराङ्मुखाः सुरगणाः संगराद् गतचेतसः ॥
162.m: The gods did not win at all there; the Dānavas were victorious. / Turning their backs on the battle, the hosts of gods lost heart.

162.s:
mām abhyetya samūcus te dehi no 'bhayakāraṇam
tān ahaṃ pratyavocaṃ vai gaṅgāṃ gacchata sarvaśaḥ //
162.d:
माम् अभ्येत्य समूचुस् ते देहि नो ऽभयकारणम्
तान् अहं प्रत्यवोचं वै गङ्गां गच्छत सर्वशः ॥
162.m: Approaching me, they said: 'Grant us cause for fearlessness.' / I replied to them: 'Go by all means to the Gaṅgā.

162.s:
tatra vai gautamītīre stutvā devaṃ maheśvaram
anapāyanirāyāsasahajānandasundaram //
162.d:
तत्र वै गौतमीतीरे स्तुत्वा देवं महेश्वरम्
अनपायनिरायाससहजानन्दसुन्दरम् ॥
162.m: There on the bank of the Gautamī, having praised the god Maheśvara, / who is imperishable, effortless, beautiful with natural bliss,

162.s:
lapsyate sarvavibudhā jayahetur maheśvarāt
tathety uktvā suragaṇāḥ stuvanti sma maheśvaram //
162.d:
लप्स्यते सर्वविबुधा जयहेतुर् महेश्वरात्
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा सुरगणाः स्तुवन्ति स्म महेश्वरम् ॥
162.m: all the gods will obtain from Maheśvara the means of victory.' / Saying 'So be it,' the hosts of gods praised Maheśvara.

162.s:
tapo 'tapyanta kecid vai nanṛtuś ca tathāpare
asnāpayaṃś ca kecic ca 'pūjayaṃś ca tathāpare //
162.d:
तपो ऽतप्यन्त केचिद् वै ननृतुश् च तथापरे
अस्नापयंश् च केचिच् च ऽपूजयंश् च तथापरे ॥
162.m: Some performed austerities, while others danced; / some bathed [his image], and others worshiped.

162.s:
tataḥ prasanno bhagavāñ śūlapāṇir maheśvaraḥ
devān athābravīt tuṣṭo vriyatāṃ yad abhīpsitam //
162.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवाञ् शूलपाणिर् महेश्वरः
देवान् अथाब्रवीत् तुष्टो व्रियतां यद् अभीप्सितम् ॥
162.m: Then pleased, the venerable Maheśvara, holder of the trident, / satisfied, said to the gods: 'Let what is desired be chosen.'

162.s:
devā ūcuḥ surapatiṃ vijayāya dadasva naḥ
puruṣaṃ paramaślāghyaṃ raṇeṣu purataḥ sthitam //
162.d:
देवा ऊचुः सुरपतिं विजयाय ददस्व नः
पुरुषं परमश्लाघ्यं रणेषु पुरतः स्थितम् ॥
162.m: The gods said: 'Grant us, O lord of the gods, for victory, / an exceedingly praiseworthy person standing at the forefront in battles,

162.s:
yadbāhubalam āśritya bhavāmaḥ sukhino vayam
tathety uvāca bhagavān devān prati maheśvaraḥ //
162.d:
यद्बाहुबलम् आश्रित्य भवामः सुखिनो वयम्
तथेत्य् उवाच भगवान् देवान् प्रति महेश्वरः ॥
162.m: relying upon the strength of whose arms we may be happy.' / 'So be it,' the venerable Maheśvara said to the gods.

162.s:
ātmanas tejasā kaścin nirmitaḥ parameṣṭhinā
manyunāmānam atyugraṃ devasainyapurogamam //
162.d:
आत्मनस् तेजसा कश्चिन् निर्मितः परमेष्ठिना
मन्युनामानम् अत्युग्रं देवसैन्यपुरोगमम् ॥
162.m: By the Supreme Lord, someone was created from his own splendor, / named Manyu, exceedingly fierce, going before the divine army.

162.s:
taṃ natvā tridaśāḥ sarve śivaṃ natvā svam ālayam
manyunā saha cābhyetya punar yuddhāya tasthire //
162.d:
तं नत्वा त्रिदशाः सर्वे शिवं नत्वा स्वम् आलयम्
मन्युना सह चाभ्येत्य पुनर् युद्धाय तस्थिरे ॥
162.m: Bowing to him and bowing to Śiva, all the thirty [gods] went to their own abode; / and having come with Manyu, they stood ready to fight again.

162.s:
yuddhe sthitvā tu danujair daiteyaiś ca mahābalaiḥ
vibudhā jātasaṃnaddhā manyum ūcuḥ puraḥ sthitāḥ //
162.d:
युद्धे स्थित्वा तु दनुजैर् दैतेयैश् च महाबलैः
विबुधा जातसंनद्धा मन्युम् ऊचुः पुरः स्थिताः ॥
162.m: Standing in battle against the Danujas and mighty Daiteyas, / the gods, having put on their armor, standing in front, spoke to Manyu:

162.s:
devā ūcuḥ
sāmarthyaṃ tava paśyāmaḥ paścād yotsyāmahe paraiḥ
tasmād darśaya cātmānaṃ manyo 'smākaṃ yuyutsatām //
162.d:
देवा ऊचुः
सामर्थ्यं तव पश्यामः पश्चाद् योत्स्यामहे परैः
तस्माद् दर्शय चात्मानं मन्यो ऽस्माकं युयुत्सताम् ॥
162.m: The gods said: / 'We shall see your ability; afterwards we will fight with the enemies. / Therefore reveal yourself, O Manyu, to us who wish to fight.'

162.s:
brahmovāca
tad devavacanaṃ śrutvā manyur āha smayann iva //
162.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् देववचनं श्रुत्वा मन्युर् आह स्मयन्न् इव ॥
162.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of the gods, Manyu said, as if smiling:

162.s:
manyur uvāca
janitā mama deveśaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvadṛk prabhuḥ
yaḥ sarvaṃ vetti sarveṣāṃ dhāmanāma manaḥsthitam //
162.d:
मन्युर् उवाच
जनिता मम देवेशः सर्वज्ञः सर्वदृक् प्रभुः
यः सर्वं वेत्ति सर्वेषां धामनाम मनःस्थितम् ॥
162.m: Manyu said: / 'My progenitor is the lord of gods, all-knowing, all-seeing master, / who knows all, the abode, name, and what is situated in the mind of all.

162.s:
naiva kaścic ca taṃ vetti yaḥ sarvaṃ vetti sarvadā
amūrtaṃ mūrtam apy etad vetti kartā jaganmayaḥ //
162.d:
नैव कश्चिच् च तं वेत्ति यः सर्वं वेत्ति सर्वदा
अमूर्तं मूर्तम् अप्य् एतद् वेत्ति कर्ता जगन्मयः ॥
162.m: No one knows him, who knows all at all times; / the creator who consists of the universe knows both this formless and this formed.'

162.s:
paro 'sau bhagavān sākṣāt tathā divy antarikṣagaḥ
kas tasya rūpaṃ yo veda kasya kartā jaganmayaḥ //
162.d:
परो ऽसौ भगवान् साक्षात् तथा दिव्य् अन्तरिक्षगः
कस् तस्य रूपं यो वेद कस्य कर्ता जगन्मयः ॥
162.m: He is transcendent, the Blessed Lord himself, and likewise moving in heaven and the intermediate space. / Who knows his form? Whose creator is he, composed of the universe?

162.s:
evaṃvidhād ahaṃ jāto māṃ kathaṃ vettum arhatha
athavā draṣṭukāmā vai bhavanto mānupaśyata //
162.d:
एवंविधाद् अहं जातो मां कथं वेत्तुम् अर्हथ
अथवा द्रष्टुकामा वै भवन्तो मानुपश्यत ॥
162.m: I am born from such as him; how could you know me? / Or, if you truly wish to see, behold me!"

162.s:
brahmovāca
ity uktvā darśayām āsa manyū rūpaṃ svakaṃ mahat
tārtīyacakṣuṣodbhūtaṃ bhavasya parameṣṭhinaḥ //
162.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा दर्शयाम् आस मन्यू रूपं स्वकं महत्
तार्तीयचक्षुषोद्भूतं भवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥
162.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, Manyu displayed his own immense form, / arisen from the third eye of Bhava, the supreme lord,

162.s:
tejasā saṃbhṛtaṃ rūpaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ tad ucyate
pauruṣaṃ puruṣeṣv eva ahaṃkāraś ca jantuṣu //
162.d:
तेजसा संभृतं रूपं यतः सर्वं तद् उच्यते
पौरुषं पुरुषेष्व् एव अहंकारश् च जन्तुषु ॥
162.m: a form filled with blazing splendor, for it is said to be all this: / the virility in men and the ego-principle in living beings,

162.s:
krodhaḥ sarvasya yo bhīma upasaṃhārakṛd bhavet
taṃ śaṃkarapratinidhiṃ jvalantaṃ nijatejasā //
162.d:
क्रोधः सर्वस्य यो भीम उपसंहारकृद् भवेत्
तं शंकरप्रतिनिधिं ज्वलन्तं निजतेजसा ॥
162.m: the terrible wrath belonging to all which brings about destruction. / Seeing that representative of Śaṅkara, blazing with his own brilliance,

162.s:
sarvāyudhadharaṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇemuḥ sarvadevatāḥ
vitresur daityadanujāḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ surāḥ //
162.d:
सर्वायुधधरं दृष्ट्वा प्रणेमुः सर्वदेवताः
वित्रेसुर् दैत्यदनुजाः कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सुराः ॥
162.m: bearing all weapons, all the gods bowed down, / while Daityas and Danujas trembled. Joining their hands in supplication, the gods,

162.s:
bhūtvā manyum athocus te tvaṃ senānīḥ prabho bhava
tvayā dattam idaṃ rājyaṃ manyo bhokṣyāmahe vayam //
162.d:
भूत्वा मन्युम् अथोचुस् ते त्वं सेनानीः प्रभो भव
त्वया दत्तम् इदं राज्यं मन्यो भोक्ष्यामहे वयम् ॥
162.m: having gathered, then addressed Manyu: "O Lord, become our general! / Given by you, O Manyu, we will enjoy this sovereignty.

162.s:
tasmāt sarveṣu kāryeṣu jetā tvaṃ jayavardhanaḥ
tvam indras tvaṃ ca varuṇo lokapālās tvam eva ca //
162.d:
तस्मात् सर्वेषु कार्येषु जेता त्वं जयवर्धनः
त्वम् इन्द्रस् त्वं च वरुणो लोकपालास् त्वम् एव च ॥
162.m: Therefore, in all undertakings you are the victor who increases victory. / You are Indra, you are Varuṇa, and you alone are the guardians of the world.

162.s:
asmāsu sarvadeveṣu praviśa tvaṃ jayāya vai
manyuḥ provāca tān sarvān vinā matto na kiṃcana //
162.d:
अस्मासु सर्वदेवेषु प्रविश त्वं जयाय वै
मन्युः प्रोवाच तान् सर्वान् विना मत्तो न किंचन ॥
162.m: Enter into us, all the gods, indeed for the sake of victory!" / Manyu said to them all: "There is nothing apart from me.

162.s:
sarveṣv antaḥ praviṣṭo 'haṃ na māṃ jānāti kaścana
sa eva bhagavān manyus tato jātaḥ pṛthak pṛthak //
162.d:
सर्वेष्व् अन्तः प्रविष्टो ऽहं न मां जानाति कश्चन
स एव भगवान् मन्युस् ततो जातः पृथक् पृथक् ॥
162.m: I have entered into the interior of all, yet no one knows me." / That very Blessed Lord Manyu was then born individually in diverse ways.

162.s:
sa eva rudrarūpī syād rudro manyuḥ śivo 'bhavat
sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva sarvaṃ vyāptaṃ hi manyunā //
162.d:
स एव रुद्ररूपी स्याद् रुद्रो मन्युः शिवो ऽभवत्
स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव सर्वं व्याप्तं हि मन्युना ॥
162.m: He indeed has the form of Rudra; Rudra is Manyu, and Śiva he became. / The immovable and the movable—all indeed was pervaded by Manyu.

162.s:
tam avāpya surāḥ sarve jayam āpuś ca saṃgare
jayo manyuś ca śauryaṃ ca īśatejaḥsamudbhavam //
162.d:
तम् अवाप्य सुराः सर्वे जयम् आपुश् च संगरे
जयो मन्युश् च शौर्यं च ईशतेजःसमुद्भवम् ॥
162.m: Having obtained him, all the gods attained victory in battle. / Victory, fury, and valor—these arise from the brilliance of the Lord.

162.s:
manyunā jayam āpyātha kṛtvā daityaiś ca saṃgamam
yathāgataṃ yayuḥ sarve manyunā parirakṣitāḥ //
162.d:
मन्युना जयम् आप्याथ कृत्वा दैत्यैश् च संगमम्
यथागतं ययुः सर्वे मन्युना परिरक्षिताः ॥
162.m: Having obtained victory through Manyu, and having encountered the Daityas, / all went as they had come, protected on all sides by Manyu.

162.s:
yatra vai gautamītīre śivam ārādhya te surāḥ
manyum āpur jayaṃ caiva manyutīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
162.d:
यत्र वै गौतमीतीरे शिवम् आराध्य ते सुराः
मन्युम् आपुर् जयं चैव मन्युतीर्थं तद् उच्यते ॥
162.m: Where on the bank of the Gautamī those gods worshipped Śiva / and obtained Manyu and victory, that is called Manyutīrtha.

162.s:
utpattiṃ ca tathā manyor yo naraḥ prayataḥ smaret
vijayo jāyate tasya na kaiścit paribhūyate //
162.d:
उत्पत्तिं च तथा मन्योर् यो नरः प्रयतः स्मरेत्
विजयो जायते तस्य न कैश्चित् परिभूयते ॥
162.m: And whatever man attentively remembers the origin of Manyu / achieves victory and is not vanquished by anyone.

162.s:
na manyutīrthasadṛśaṃ pāvanaṃ hi mahāmune
yatra sākṣān manyurūpī sarvadā śaṃkaraḥ sthitaḥ
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca smaraṇaṃ sarvakāmadam //
162.d:
न मन्युतीर्थसदृशं पावनं हि महामुने
यत्र साक्षान् मन्युरूपी सर्वदा शंकरः स्थितः
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च स्मरणं सर्वकामदम् ॥
162.m: There is no purifying place equal to Manyutīrtha, O great sage, / where Śaṅkara himself constantly abides in the form of Manyu; / bathing, giving gifts, and remembrance there fulfill all desires.

163.s:
brahmovāca
sārasvataṃ nāma tīrthaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham
bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṝṇāṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
163.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सारस्वतं नाम तीर्थं सर्वकामप्रदं शुभम्
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नॄणां सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
163.m: Brahmā said: / There is an auspicious tīrtha named Sārasvata, which grants all desires, / giving worldly enjoyment and liberation to men, destroying all sins,

163.s:
sarvarogapraśamanaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam
tatremaṃ śṛṇu vṛttāntaṃ vistareṇātha nārada //
163.d:
सर्वरोगप्रशमनं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम्
तत्रेमं शृणु वृत्तान्तं विस्तरेणाथ नारद ॥
163.m: pacifying all diseases, and granting all perfections. / Hear now in detail the account of that place, O Nārada.

163.s:
puṣpotkaṭāt pūrvabhāge parvato lokaviśrutaḥ
śubhro nāma giriśreṣṭho gautamyā dakṣiṇe taṭe //
163.d:
पुष्पोत्कटात् पूर्वभागे पर्वतो लोकविश्रुतः
शुभ्रो नाम गिरिश्रेष्ठो गौतम्या दक्षिणे तटे ॥
163.m: To the east of Puṣpotkaṭa there is a world-renowned mountain, / the best of mountains named Śubhra, on the southern bank of the Gautamī.

163.s:
śākalya iti vikhyāto muniḥ paramanaiṣṭhikaḥ
tasmiñ śubhre puṇyagirau tapas tepe hy anuttamam //
163.d:
शाकल्य इति विख्यातो मुनिः परमनैष्ठिकः
तस्मिञ् शुभ्रे पुण्यगिरौ तपस् तेपे ह्य् अनुत्तमम् ॥
163.m: A sage known as Śākalya, completely steadfast in his vows, / performed unequaled austerities on that sacred mountain Śubhra.

163.s:
tapasyantaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ gautamītīram āśritam
sarve bhūtagaṇā nityaṃ praṇamanti stuvanti tam //
163.d:
तपस्यन्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं गौतमीतीरम् आश्रितम्
सर्वे भूतगणा नित्यं प्रणमन्ति स्तुवन्ति तम् ॥
163.m: All the hosts of beings constantly bow to and praise that best of twice-born men / who was performing austerities, resting on the bank of the Gautamī,

163.s:
agniśuśrūṣaṇaparaṃ vedādhyayanatatparam
ṛṣigandharvasumanaḥsevite tatra parvate //
163.d:
अग्निशुश्रूषणपरं वेदाध्ययनतत्परम्
ऋषिगन्धर्वसुमनःसेविते तत्र पर्वते ॥
163.m: intent on tending the sacred fire, devoted to the study of the Vedas, / on that mountain frequented by ṛṣis, gandharvas, and gods.

163.s:
tasmin girau mahāpuṇye devadvijabhayaṃkaraḥ
yajñadveṣī brahmahantā paraśur nāma rākṣasaḥ //
163.d:
तस्मिन् गिरौ महापुण्ये देवद्विजभयंकरः
यज्ञद्वेषी ब्रह्महन्ता परशुर् नाम राक्षसः ॥
163.m: On that exceedingly sacred mountain, a rākṣasa named Paraśu, / a terror to gods and twice-born, a hater of sacrifices, a slayer of brahmins,

163.s:
kāmarūpī vicarati nānārūpadharo vane
kṣaṇaṃ ca brahmarūpeṇa kadācid vyāghrarūpadhṛk //
163.d:
कामरूपी विचरति नानारूपधरो वने
क्षणं च ब्रह्मरूपेण कदाचिद् व्याघ्ररूपधृक् ॥
163.m: able to change form at will, roamed through the forest assuming various forms: / one moment in the form of a brahmin, at times bearing the form of a tiger,

163.s:
kadācid devarūpeṇa kadācit paśurūpadhṛk
kadācit pramadārūpaḥ kadācin mṛgarūpataḥ //
163.d:
कदाचिद् देवरूपेण कदाचित् पशुरूपधृक्
कदाचित् प्रमदारूपः कदाचिन् मृगरूपतः ॥
163.m: at times in the form of a god, at times assuming the form of a beast, / at times having the form of a woman, at times having the appearance of a deer,

163.s:
kadācid bālarūpeṇa evaṃ carati pāpakṛt
yatrāste brāhmaṇo vidvāñ śākalyo munisattamaḥ //
163.d:
कदाचिद् बालरूपेण एवं चरति पापकृत्
यत्रास्ते ब्राह्मणो विद्वाञ् शाकल्यो मुनिसत्तमः ॥
163.m: and at times in the form of a child—thus did the evil-doer wander. / Where the learned brāhmaṇa Śākalya, the best of sages, dwelt,

163.s:
tam āyāti mahāpāpī paraśū rākṣasādhamaḥ
śuciṣmantaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ paraśur nityam eva ca //
163.d:
तम् आयाति महापापी परशू राक्षसाधमः
शुचिष्मन्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं परशुर् नित्यम् एव च ॥
163.m: there came that great sinner, Paraśu, the lowest of rākṣasas. / And Paraśu was constantly [trying] to carry off and kill

163.s:
netuṃ hantuṃ pravṛtto 'pi na śaśāka sa pāpakṛt
sa kadācid dvijaśreṣṭho devān abhyarcya yatnataḥ //
163.d:
नेतुं हन्तुं प्रवृत्तो ऽपि न शशाक स पापकृत्
स कदाचिद् द्विजश्रेष्ठो देवान् अभ्यर्च्य यत्नतः ॥
163.m: that pure, radiant, best of twice-born men, but the evil-doer was unable. / Once, having diligently worshipped the gods,

163.s:
bhoktukāmaḥ kilāyātas tatrāyāt paraśur mune
brahmarūpadharo bhūtvā śithilaḥ palito 'balī
kanyām ādāya kāṃcic ca śākalyaṃ vākyam abravīt //
163.d:
भोक्तुकामः किलायातस् तत्रायात् परशुर् मुने
ब्रह्मरूपधरो भूत्वा शिथिलः पलितो ऽबली
कन्याम् आदाय कांचिच् च शाकल्यं वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
163.m: that best of twice-born men came desiring to eat; then Paraśu came there, O sage, / having assumed the form of a brahmin, feeble, gray-haired, and frail, / and bringing a certain maiden, he spoke these words to Śākalya:

163.s:
paraśur uvāca
bhojanasyārthinaṃ viddhi māṃ ca kanyām imāṃ dvija
ātithyakāle saṃprāptaṃ kṛtakṛtyo 'si mānada //
163.d:
परशुर् उवाच
भोजनस्यार्थिनं विद्धि मां च कन्याम् इमां द्विज
आतिथ्यकाले संप्राप्तं कृतकृत्यो ऽसि मानद ॥
163.m: Paraśu said: / "Know me and this maiden, O twice-born, to be desirous of food, / arrived at the time for hospitality; you have accomplished your duty, O giver of honor!

163.s:
ta eva dhanyā loke 'smin yeṣām atithayo gṛhāt
pūrṇābhilāṣā niryānti jīvanto 'pi mṛtāḥ pare //
163.d:
त एव धन्या लोके ऽस्मिन् येषाम् अतिथयो गृहात्
पूर्णाभिलाषा निर्यान्ति जीवन्तो ऽपि मृताः परे ॥
163.m: Blessed indeed are those in this world from whose house guests depart / with their desires fulfilled; the others, even while living, are dead.

163.s:
bhojane tūpaviṣṭe tu ātmārthaṃ kalpitaṃ tu yat
atithibhyas tu yo dadyād dattā tena vasuṃdharā //
163.d:
भोजने तूपविष्टे तु आत्मार्थं कल्पितं तु यत्
अतिथिभ्यस् तु यो दद्याद् दत्ता तेन वसुंधरा ॥
163.m: When one has sat down to eat, whoever gives to guests / that which was prepared for himself, by him the earth is given!"

163.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā tu śākalyo dadāmīty evam abravīt
āsane copaveśyāthājñānāt taṃ paraśuṃ dvijam //
163.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा तु शाकल्यो ददामीत्य् एवम् अब्रवीत्
आसने चोपवेश्याथाज्ञानात् तं परशुं द्विजम् ॥
163.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard this, Śākalya said, "I will give." / Then, having seated that twice-born Paraśu on a seat, out of ignorance,

163.s:
yathānyāyaṃ pūjayitvā śākalyo bhojanaṃ dadau
āpośanaṃ kare kṛtvā paraśur vākyam abravīt //
163.d:
यथान्यायं पूजयित्वा शाकल्यो भोजनं ददौ
आपोशनं करे कृत्वा परशुर् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
163.m: and having honored him properly, Śākalya offered him food. / Having performed the ceremonial sipping of water in his hand, Paraśu spoke these words:

163.s:
paraśur uvāca
dūrād abhyāgataṃ śrāntam anugacchanti devatāḥ
tasmiṃs tṛpte tu tṛptāḥ syur atṛpte tu viparyayaḥ //
163.d:
परशुर् उवाच
दूराद् अभ्यागतं श्रान्तम् अनुगच्छन्ति देवताः
तस्मिंस् तृप्ते तु तृप्ताः स्युर् अतृप्ते तु विपर्ययः ॥
163.m: Paraśu said: / "The deities follow a guest who has arrived weary from afar; / when he is satisfied, they are satisfied, but when he is unsatisfied, the opposite occurs.

163.s:
atithiś cāpavādī ca dvāv etau viśvabāndhavau
apavādī haret pāpam atithiḥ svargasaṃkramaḥ //
163.d:
अतिथिश् चापवादी च द्वाव् एतौ विश्वबान्धवौ
अपवादी हरेत् पापम् अतिथिः स्वर्गसंक्रमः ॥
163.m: A guest and a slanderer—these two are the kin of all: / the slanderer takes away sin, and the guest is a bridge to heaven.

163.s:
abhyāgataṃ pathi śrāntaṃ sāvajñaṃ yo 'bhivīkṣate
tatkṣaṇād eva naśyanti tasya dharmayaśaḥśriyaḥ //
163.d:
अभ्यागतं पथि श्रान्तं सावज्ञं यो ऽभिवीक्षते
तत्क्षणाद् एव नश्यन्ति तस्य धर्मयशःश्रियः ॥
163.m: Whoever looks contemptuously upon a guest arrived weary from the road, / in that very instant his dharma, fame, and fortune perish.

163.s:
tasmād abhyāgataḥ śrānto yāce 'haṃ tvāṃ dvijottama
dāsyase yadi me kāmaṃ tad bhokṣye 'haṃ na cānyathā //
163.d:
तस्माद् अभ्यागतः श्रान्तो याचे ऽहं त्वां द्विजोत्तम
दास्यसे यदि मे कामं तद् भोक्ष्ये ऽहं न चान्यथा ॥
163.m: Therefore, having arrived weary, I make a request of you, O best of twice-born: / if you will grant my desire, then I shall eat, and not otherwise."

163.s:
brahmovāca
dattam ity eva śākalyo bhuṅkṣvety evāha rākṣasam
tataḥ provāca paraśur ahaṃ rākṣasasattamaḥ //
163.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दत्तम् इत्य् एव शाकल्यो भुङ्क्ष्वेत्य् एवाह राक्षसम्
ततः प्रोवाच परशुर् अहं राक्षससत्तमः ॥
163.m: Brahmā said: / Saying "It is given," Śākalya said to the rākṣasa, "Eat!" / Then Paraśu said: "I am the greatest of rākṣasas;

163.s:
nāhaṃ dvijas tava ripur na vṛddhaḥ palitaḥ kṛśaḥ
bahūni me vyatītāni varṣāṇi tvāṃ prapaśyataḥ //
163.d:
नाहं द्विजस् तव रिपुर् न वृद्धः पलितः कृशः
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि वर्षाणि त्वां प्रपश्यतः ॥
163.m: I am not a twice-born, but your enemy, not old, gray-haired, or lean. / Many years have passed for me watching you.

163.s:
śuṣyanti mama gātrāṇi grīṣme svalpodakaṃ yathā
tasmān neṣye sānugaṃ tvāṃ bhakṣayiṣye dvijottama //
163.d:
शुष्यन्ति मम गात्राणि ग्रीष्मे स्वल्पोदकं यथा
तस्मान् नेष्ये सानुगं त्वां भक्षयिष्ये द्विजोत्तम ॥
163.m: My limbs are drying up like shallow water in the hot season. / Therefore I shall carry you off along with your followers and eat you, O best of twice-born!"

163.s:
brahmovāca
śrutvā paraśuvākyaṃ tac chākalyo vākyam abravīt //
163.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
श्रुत्वा परशुवाक्यं तच् छाकल्यो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
163.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of Paraśu, Śākalya spoke these words:

163.s:
śākalya uvāca
ye mahākulasaṃbhūtā vijñātasakalāgamāḥ
tat pratiśrutam abhyeti na jātv atra viparyayam //
163.d:
शाकल्य उवाच
ये महाकुलसंभूता विज्ञातसकलागमाः
तत् प्रतिश्रुतम् अभ्येति न जात्व् अत्र विपर्ययम् ॥
163.m: Śākalya said: / "Those who are born of great families and know all the traditional texts— / their promise is upheld; it never turns into its opposite here.

163.s:
yathocitaṃ kuru sakhe tathāpi śṛṇu me vacaḥ
nihantum apy udyateṣu vaktavyaṃ hitam uttamaiḥ //
163.d:
यथोचितं कुरु सखे तथापि शृणु मे वचः
निहन्तुम् अप्य् उद्यतेषु वक्तव्यं हितम् उत्तमैः ॥
